title: Canonical catalog: 38 tool names + 25 resource URIs
description:
# Task: Enumerate all 38 AM-Rust tool names + 25 resource URIs (canonical catalog)

## Background
Parity is name-for-name. Agents and conformance need a single first-party catalog committed in-repo so implementers do not reverse-engineer from memory or risk license issues with AM-Rust sources.

## What
1. Produce `docs/parity/am-rust-tool-catalog.md` (or `tests/conformance/CATALOG.md`) listing:
   - All 38 tools by cluster with exact names, required args, return shape summary
   - All 25 MCP resource URIs + schema summaries
2. Cross-check counts: 4+6+5+4+5+2+4+5+3 = 38
3. Flag any ADR abbreviation gaps (macros names especially underspecified in ADR)
4. This catalog is the source of truth for `bd-led.7.2` and `bd-77u.1` fixtures

## Why users (agents) care
Shell-only agents and MCP clients need identical surfaces. Missing one tool = integration break.

## Success
- Catalog committed; CI can count tools == 38 and resources == 25
- Every Phase-1 mailbox bead references tools by exact name from catalog

## Does NOT require crates
Can start in parallel with workspace reshape (same as fixtures).
close_reason: docs/parity/am-rust-tool-catalog.md committed: 38 tools (9 clusters) + 25 resource URIs, counts verified programmatically, derived from public AM-Rust interface (README + #[tool]/#[resource] attrs), no test code vendored. ADR gaps flagged (macros names).

title: Buzz + AgentMail comparative study (2026-08-07) — doc + bead tree
description:
# Buzz + AgentMail comparative study (2026-08-07)

Full study at docs/notes/2026-08-07-buzz-agentmail-comparison.md.

## Verdict
toron matches agentmail on the 38-tool mailbox parity (bd-96a catalogues intentional
divergences). toron matches/exceeds buzz on adopted primitives (kind-as-dispatch, relay
pipeline, @mention dispatch, YAML workflows, NIP-29 channels, presence) + uniquely wins
on crypto identity (Schnorr npub), E2E DMs (NIP-17 gift-wrap), federation, durable
workflow resumption (Resonate — buzz WF-08 unbuilt).

toron LAGS on operational surface (doctor reconstruct/archive-scan, share/export, golden
capture, ATC, robot depth, TUI) and the Forge (NIP-34 git events).

## Quick-win beads filed (this session)
- bd-bzu (P1) mention coalescing — Buzz L2 [highest leverage]
- bd-nsv (P1) workflow loop-prevention hardening — Buzz L5 [correctness]
- bd-jwa (P2) doctor reconstruct — AM A1
- bd-n87 (P2) bound workflow guard evaluation — Buzz L4
- bd-o1h (P2) operator-bypass (Overseer) — AM A6

## Research epics filed
- ATC learning loop (AM A5) — bd-<atc>
- Forge NIP-34 (Buzz L3) — bd-<forge>

## Key insight
toron is architecturally ahead (Nostr-native + federation + durable + local-first),
operationally behind. Path: ship 5 quick wins → 5 medium → decide ATC vs Forge.
close_reason: Study delivered: docs/notes/2026-08-07-buzz-agentmail-comparison.md + ADR-0004 (accepted) framing items 1-5 as ships, 11+12 as deferred non-goals. Action beads unblocked from this parent (dep removed) so they're ready; ADR-0004 is now the governing frame, not this bead.

title: SUPERSEDED: SC-14 split into 14a/14b
description:
# SC-14 — Disaster recovery + negentropy rejoin [P1/P2] (G11/A5)

## (a) SQLite lost [P1]
Delete SQLite → rebuild projection from Git archive → state consistent with prior tool queries.

## (b) Bus/relay rejoin [P1/P2]
Lose bus state → rejoin via **NIP-77 negentropy delta** from in-process second relay → only missing events transferred → consistent.

## Assert
- either source alone rebuilds
- negentropy transfers **delta only** (bandwidth < full replay)
- signed events re-verified on rejoin
- no real network; virtual second relay

## Implementation note
Part (a) can gate v1; part (b) may land with RelayBus/negentropy beads but still under toron-e2e SC-14.
close_reason: Split into SC-14a (Git rebuild, v1) and SC-14b (negentropy). Avoided blocking v1 on federation stack.

## What

close_reason: Ephemeral presence 20001 + persona packs. nostr/presence.rs: PresenceState (Idle/Working/Blocked/Done/Unknown, herdr-aligned), PresencePayload, build_presence_event (kind-20001, NO project scoping — system-level, global sub receives), parse. bus/presence.rs: PresenceBroker — subscribes kind-20001, last-heartbeat-wins keyed by pubkey, expiry on stale (TTL), lossy live broadcast (review carve-out: presence is the canonical dropping-channel consumer), expire_stale GC. InProcessBus::publish now treats ephemeral kinds (20000-29999, is_ephemeral_kind) as broadcast-only — NOT stored in SQLite (ADR: never projected; fanout refactored to shared fn). identity.rs: AgentProfile extended with versioned PersonaPack (version/name/system_prompt), backward-compatible optional. 10 presence tests + ephemeral-not-stored bus test. Workspace 351 tests green, clippy -D warnings 0, fmt clean. Ripple: added persona:None to 7 peer test/tool AgentProfile literals (mailbox x6 + toron-mcp x2) — mechanical, flagged. Projection skip of 20001 notified to oc-d.

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — CHANNEL CHOICE (aligns with the bd-led.3.2 lossless rule):

Presence (kind-20001) is ephemeral + loss-tolerant, so it is the CANONICAL consumer for the DROPPING `tokio::broadcast` channel. A missed heartbeat just means stale presence until the next one — no data loss, because presence is never projected to SQLite/Git by definition.

- DO put presence on the bus `broadcast` (lossy is fine here — it's the explicit carve-out from the bd-led.3.2 review).
- DO NOT put presence on the lossless projection channel (would defeat "not stored").
- The projection (bd-led.4.4) must EXPLICITLY ignore kind-20001 (skip index + skip Git) — add that to its filter.
- Subscribe the presence broadcaster to the bus broadcast; consumers (an MCP presence resource, or herdr-replacement polling) tolerate gaps via "last heartbeat wins + expiry on stale".

title: toron herdr protocol v19: bump HDR_PROTOCOL 18->19 + conform wire structs
description:
# toron herdr protocol v19 bump (flywheel-side already v19; toron lags)

## Problem

toron-core pins `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 18` (crates/toron-core/src/backend/herdr.rs:29) while the live herdr daemon reports protocol 19 (`herdr api schema --json` → `protocol: 19`). flywheel's verify-0001.sh gate greps toron-core's pin and FAILS until it is >= 19 (escalated from flywheel bd-8vg; the toron-side tracker never picked it up — this bead closes that gap). flywheel itself already consumes v19 (bd-protocol-v19-bump-dy4).

## What to do

1. Verify toron-core's herdr wire structs against the live v19 schema (`herdr api schema --json`). The v19 deltas (from flywheel's own bump bead) are:
   - AgentInfo.agent_status is NON-Option in v19 (toron already matches)
   - WorkspaceInfo +number, +focused, +active_tab_id (toron already has these)
   - PaneInfo +terminal_id, +focused (toron's PaneInfo at herdr.rs:108 has ONLY pane_id/title/cwd/agent_status — MISSING)
   - WorktreeInfo: workspace_id → open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools (toron's WorktreeInfo at herdr.rs:117 has worktree_id/workspace_id/branch/label — MISMATCH)
2. Fix the structs that do not conform (PaneInfo terminal_id/focused; WorktreeInfo open_workspace_id + booleans per live schema).
3. Bump `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL` 18 → 19.
4. Update module doc + any protocol-comment references (18 → 19).
5. Verify: a live round-trip against the running herdr daemon (agent.list / workspace.list / pane.list) parses; `cargo test` green; the flywheel verify-0001.sh gate goes GREEN (flywheel path-depends on this repo: ~/workspace/toron).

## Success criteria

- `pub const HDR_PROTOCOL: u64 = 19` in toron-core.
- PaneInfo/WorktreeInfo conform to live v19 schema (field-for-field).
- Live herdr round-trip parses (herdr up, agent.list etc).
- toron `cargo test` passes.
- flywheel `bash docs/decisions/_scripts/verify-0001.sh` passes after this lands.

## Considerations

- The herdr client is the SHARED client across flywheel + toron (ADR-0003 Decision 3A) — sc-fw test asserts exactly one `fn agent_prompt`. Do not duplicate client logic; only fix the structs + pin here.
- Backwards compat: v19 adds fields; existing v18 consumers are unaffected. Wire structs are Deserialize-only here.
- TDD: write/extend a fixture-based parse test (live schema trimmed fixture like flywheel's tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) before/with the struct changes.
close_reason: v19 conformed: PaneInfo field-for-field (+terminal_id/workspace_id/tab_id/focused/agent_status non-Option/revision + agent_session/scroll/etc), WorktreeInfo -> open_workspace_id + 4 worktree bools (path/is_bare/is_detached/is_prunable/is_linked_worktree/label/branch); HDR_PROTOCOL 18->19; fixture tests (crates/toron-core/tests/fixtures/herdr-schema-v19.json) green (17 backend tests); full toron-core suite 323 passed (3 bd-5icg in-flight failures = Crew 2's, not mine); flywheel verify-0001.sh PASSED; live round-trip (agent.list/workspace.list/pane.list via typed client) passed against running daemon; clippy -D warnings: 2 pre-existing errors in untouched mailbox files (surface.rs:324, mod.rs:177), zero from this change

title: toron: renew_file_reservations expiry-doubles bug (FIXED)
description:
TORON FIX — commit b08f495
Real-e2e probe: renew advanced expires_ts_us from 1786022764000000 to
3572045556000000 (2x). Root cause: reservations.rs renew treated the ABSOLUTE
epoch expires_ts_us as a RELATIVE duration and re-added to now, double-counting
elapsed time.

FIX: new_expiry = old_abs + extend_secs (absolute), stored as relative TTL
(new_abs - now) so NIP-40 expiration lands at the correct absolute time.
Test test_renew_and_release green.
close_reason: commit b08f495 - renew extends absolute expiry; test_renew_and_release green

title: toron read-state: read_ts projection + honest unread_only filtering
description:
# toron read-state (read receipts in the projection)

## Problem

toron's `fetch_inbox` treats `unread_only` as a documented NO-OP (`messages` branch in messaging.rs:271-278: "Unread-only filtering needs the projection read-state; the pipeline-level dedup treats everything as fresh on first read"). There is no per-recipient read_ts anywhere in the projection, so:
- callers cannot query "what's new since I last looked"
- the AM-parity `mark_message_read` MCP tool exists but writes nothing the projection reads
- flywheel's mail digest/wake uses the `recent` proxy (importance high|urgent) instead of true unread

## What to do

1. Add a per-recipient read-state: a `read_ts` (or per-(message,agent) read receipt) that `mark_message_read`/acknowledge paths WRITE and `fetch_inbox(unread_only: true)` FILTERS on.
   - Where: the SQLite index (`messages` table + a recipient-reads table, or a read_ts column per recipient row in the projection), consistent with the SqliteProjectionSink model (unwrap.rs:413+).
   - The bus/replay path has no read state by nature (events are immutable) — read state is a PROJECTION concern; must be rebuilt/derived deterministically.
2. Wire `mark_message_read` (and the fetch path, per AM parity "fetch marks read") to write the state.
3. Make `unread_only: true` actually filter (fetch_inbox + the surface InboxQuery path + the MCP layer).
4. Expose unread count where useful (e.g. the existing tool response or a small addition) — do not break the existing response shapes.

## Success criteria

- `fetch_inbox(unread_only: true)` returns only messages not yet read by the requesting agent (was: everything).
- `mark_message_read` on a message makes it disappear from the unread-only view.
- Read state survives process restart (persisted, not in-memory-only).
- AM-parity tests (live or unit) cover: mark-read → unread-only fetch excludes it.
- `cargo test` green; no regression in the non-unread path.

## Considerations

- Determinism: read state is projection state, NOT event state — do not write it into Nostr events. The bus replay must converge (read state is a local projection; deleting the index and rebuilding must not re-derive read state from events — document this: read receipts are lost on index rebuild, acceptable for now, or persist alongside the archive).
- Match AM-Rust semantics: AM's fetch_inbox marks returned messages read by default (that is what flywheel's digest historically collided with). Decide + document: does `fetch_inbox` (no args) mark read, or only `mark_message_read`? Prefer explicit `mark_message_read` only (fetch stays read-only) — this is the safer default and keeps the flywheel digest honest.
- Surface consistency: MailSurface `InboxQuery` already carries `unread_only` — the leaf/facade plumbing is done; only the projection needs the real behavior.
- TDD: unit test the projection filter + mark-read round trip before wiring the MCP surface.
close_reason: read-state projection: message_reads table (migration 0002), mark_message_read/acknowledge_message write read_ts, fetch_inbox(unread_only:true) filters, read_ts_us exposed on MCP inbox rows (additive). fetch_inbox stays read-only (design decision). Unit tests: mark-read->unread-only excludes, survives restart, ack implies read, no-pool degrade. cargo test toron-core 326P + toron-mcp 28P, clippy -D warnings green (--no-deps --lib), conformance 5P.

title: P3: NIP-09 deletion handling on projection sinks (probe #6)
description:
## Project context (ADR-0008 review charter)

toron = Nostr-native Tokio multi-backend agent mailbox (5 crates, 45,609 LOC:
toron-core 22,152 / toron-mcp 6,574 / toron-workflow 7,618 / toron-cli 4,340 /
toron-e2e 4,925). ADRs 0003-0007 marked implementation-complete. ADR-0008
(`docs/decisions/0008-comprehensive-codebase-review-charter.md`, Rev 1,
accepted 2026-08-09) charters a de novo adversarial review to verify the
ADR-0007 Soundness Ledger S1-S9 are genuinely green in code (not paper) and
surface material bugs / refactor debt / perf gaps across all layers.

Measured baseline (2026-08-09, reproducible): `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in
every crate root + 23+ files (0 real unsafe; `rg -n "unsafe" crates/*/src |
rg -v "forbid\(unsafe_code\)"` = 5 hits all doc comments); 0 real-src panic!
(all 35 hits in #[cfg(test)]); 219 unwrap() + 984 expect() + 67
unwrap_or(0)/default + 548 clone() in src; 102 Mutex/RwLock mentions (52 real
instantiations), 122 .lock() sites, 1324 .await sites; 574 tests (335 #[test]
+ 239 #[tokio::test]), 2 #[ignore]; cargo check clean; clippy 16 lints.

Round-1 opencode debate (Adversary 1 "oc" + Adversary 2 "oc2", DeepSeek V4
Flash): BOTH AGREE-WITH-CHANGES. oc RAN all 11 Soundness Ledger gate tests -
ALL GREEN. "Fully implemented 0003-0007" SURVIVES for the ledger. 20 Change
Agenda items resolved 19 ACCEPT / 1 REJECT in
`docs/review/0008-captain-resolution.md`.

Captain decisions: (1) all tracks P0-P6; (2) Nostr native = production,
agent-mail = compiled fallback (must pass D8.2); (3) toron only - flywheel
boundary documented NOT edited; (4) BATCH fix (RED->GREEN in one pass);
(5) API reshape allowed if future-proofs; (6) correctness AND performance;
(7) debate-governed. Sequencing: P0 -> P1 -> P2 -> P3 -> P4 -> P5 -> P6 ->
batch-fix-pass.

## This task (P3 probe #6 - NIP-09 deletion handling on projection sinks)

Probe 6 of the P3 track (bd-p3-crypto-giftwrap-cfho) had NO leaf bead - this
is that leaf. Verify NIP-09 (deletion request) events are honored on BOTH
projection sinks: a delete of a message must be reflected in sqlite + git,
and the delete itself must be replay/dedup-safe.

## Method
1. Trace NIP-09 `kind:5` / `kind:62` (delete/undelete) handling: does the
   unwrap pipeline special-case them, or are they projected as ordinary
   events? Name fn + line per sink.
2. For each sink: is a deleted message actually removed/tombstoned, or does
   it linger (deleted-but-still-readable = parity hole)?
3. Is there a NIP-09 replay hazard (deleting a message that was already
   deleted, or delete-vs-insert ordering)?

## Success criteria
Findings table: sink x NIP-09 handling x line x verdict (GREEN/RED). If a
sink ignores NIP-09 -> P0 finding + RED test in batch (deleted message must
not be readable).

## Considerations
Cross-refs: p3-replay-dedup-per-sink-nve6 (dedup mechanism per sink),
p3-projection-atomicity-rtjz (sink ordering/failure). NIP-09 is part of the
ADR-0003 "federatable threads" claim - a deleted DM that stays readable on
one store voids it.

title: gift_wrap: verify NIP-17 created_at randomization (seal+wrap, not rumor) actually applied
description:
# F4 — NIP-17 created_at randomization: verify the right timestamp is randomized

## Evidence of defect (v1.0.0 @ fc96a23)
`crates/toron-core/src/nostr/gift_wrap.rs`:
- Contains 2 `Timestamp::now()` call sites + 4 `randomize` mentions + 2 `2 days` mentions.
- The ADR (Verification bullet G7 + Phase-1 federation note) states: **'NIP-17 randomizes created_at on seal AND wrap (up to 2 days back) — envelope time is NOT mail timeline.'** The rumor `created_at` (+`ts_ms` tag) is the mail timeline; the seal + wrap timestamps MUST be randomized for metadata-hiding.

## What needs verifying (not assuming defect — confirming witness)
1. The `Timestamp::now()` calls are on the RUMOR (correct — rumor time = mail timeline, ordered by G7) OR on the seal/wrap (WRONG — should be randomized).
2. The seal (kind 13) and gift wrap (kind 1059) get `created_at = now() - random(0..2 days)`.
3. SC-2/SC-3 tests assert the metadata-hiding property (envelope time ≠ mail time).

## Soundness gap (if the randomization is missing)
- **Privacy preservation broken**: a passive observer can correlate wrap arrival time with send time, defeating the NIP-17 metadata-hiding that the ADR claims as a parity-superiority feature over AM-Rust.
- The 'NIP-17-only crypto' federation privacy guarantee depends on this.

## Minimum acceptable fix
- Audit gift_wrap.rs: confirm `Timestamp::now()` is ONLY used for the rumor, and the seal + wrap get `Timestamp::now() - Duration::from_secs(random(0..172800))` (2 days).
- Add a unit test: build a wrap, assert `wrap.created_at <= now()` AND `wrap.created_at >= now() - 2 days`, AND `wrap.created_at != seal.created_at` (independent randomization), AND `rumor.created_at` is the unrandomized send time.
- If already correct, close with witness citation (the audit IS the fix — makes the invariant explicit + tested).

## Do NOT broaden into
- Changing the 2-day window (NIP-17 mandate).
- Adding timing-attack defenses (separate concern).

## Remediation posture
Narrow. Either confirm + test (if already correct) or apply the randomization + test (if missing).
close_reason: AUDIT CLOSED — non-material, witness already present. gift_wrap() delegates to nostr_sdk EventBuilder::gift_wrap (line 92) which performs NIP-17 created_at randomization internally per the SDK contract. Witness: test_wrap_randomizes_created_at (gift_wrap.rs:286) asserts wrap.created_at <= now AND wrap.created_at + 172800 (2 days) >= now AND wrap.created_at != rumor.created_at. The 2 Timestamp::now() calls in the file are on the RUMOR path (correct — rumor time = mail timeline per G7). No code change needed; the audit IS the fix.

title: Parity shape catalog: identity-model + field divergences (npub vs id; ts_us vs ISO; event-id returns)
description:
# F8 — intentional-but-catalogued parity shape divergences (real-e2e probe)

These are NOT bugs (toron = Nostr-native by design) but must be documented so integration tests know what to expect. Catalogued by the 3-agent real-e2e opencode probe (2026-08-06).

## Identity model (biggest divergence — EXPECTED, do NOT change)
- toron returns npub/key_path/profile_event_id (Nostr identity); AM-Rust returns integer id + registration_token (no npub). Every identity op differs in response shape. toron is crypto-native per ADR-0003.

## Field-shape divergences surfaced (per op)
- whois/list_agents: toron has npub, no id/capabilities/recent_commits/inception_ts; AM has id/capabilities, no npub. Timestamps: last_active_ts_us (int us) vs last_active_ts (ISO).
- resolve_pane_identity: toron returns empty success on no-pane; AM hard-errors.
- cleanup_pane_identities: [] vs {removed_count, removed_paths}.
- request_contact: toron drops reason arg; AM stores + returns it. toron lacks expires_ts.
- set_contact_policy: toron returns bare event-id hex string; AM returns {agent, policy}. NO read API surfaces contact_policy on toron (invisible after set).
- summarize_thread: toron flat message_count; AM nested summary.total_messages.
- file_reservation release: toron {released:1}; AM {released:1, released_at}.
- send_message: payload field names differ (wrap-id vs AM numeric delivery id).
- Naming policy: AM enforces adjective+noun (rejects PiAmA); toron accepts arbitrary names (toron MORE permissive — arguably an advantage).
- fetch_inbox: toron entries lack read_ts/kind shape AM has.
- reply_message: toron requires subject; AM optional subject_prefix.
- search_messages: param names differ (since/until vs date_start/date_end).
- health_check: toron 2-field {archive,bus}; AM deep {status,health_level,verdicts,queues,disk}.

## Recommendation
Add docs/parity/known-divergences.md (or extend the catalog) enumerating these so the parity test asserts structurally-equivalent-where-required, not byte-identical. Do NOT chase byte-parity on Nostr-vs-sqlite models.

## AM-side behaviors (not toron faults)
- acquire/renew/release_build_slot: AM disabled in this env (needs WORKTREES_ENABLED); toron works.
- search_messages on AM runs degraded (search_index_stale); toron returns [] (no test data).
- AM conflict-check requires normalized /private/tmp path; toron accepts both /tmp and /private/tmp (toron advantage).

title: ADR-0005: Orchestration Tier (umbrella)
description:
# ADR-0005: Orchestration Tier — Profiles, Workflows, Stages, Smart Cron, Flexible Engine

## Why this exists (the captain's churn, resolved)
After ADR-0003 (Nostr mailbox fabric) and ADR-0004 (5 hardening ships), the captain reported **churn** around three unresolved questions:
1. Where does the orchestration vocabulary live (toron vs flywheel)?
2. The workflow engine is static AND swallows failures (no fan-out/branch/retry, no run-failure propagation).
3. Cron is fire-and-forget (the captain's hand-built docker-auto-upgrade + agent-reach-upgrade sagas have no unified, self-reporting successor).

ADR-0005 resolves all three and is **Accepted** (2-round opencode adversarial review + 3 captain amendments + 1 protocol audit). Source of truth: `docs/decisions/0005-orchestration-layer.md` (1181 lines). **These beads replace the ADR as the executable plan — they are self-contained; do not consult the ADR mid-implementation.**

## The core decision (tier model)
Execution **substrate** stays in toron; orchestration **vocabulary** goes to flywheel. One-way dependency: `flywheel → toron-workflow → toron-core` (the first arrow is NEW — P3 wires it). Standalone peer mode (two agents + a triage workflow, no orchestrator) is a CI-tested contract (`sc11`); the engine must work with no flywheel.

| Tier | Owner |
|---|---|
| 0 Identity/Transport | toron-core::nostr+bus |
| 1 Mailbox fabric + ONE Backend trait | toron-core (P1 unifies the duplicated trait) |
| 2 Execution substrate (engine, failure-path, invoke, control-flow) | toron-workflow |
| 3 Orchestration (profiles, workflows catalog, stages, smart cron, squads, runs) | flywheel |
| 4 Surfaces | toron-mcp (frozen 38 tools) + toron-cli + flywheel-cli |

## The invariants every bead obeys (non-negotiable)
1. **No new kind.** Reuse ADR-0003 frozen registry (30010-14, 30031/32, 20001, 43001-06, 46001-12).
2. **No new MCP tool.** 38-tool surface frozen. New vocabulary = CLI only.
3. **No dependency inversion.** flywheel → toron-workflow → toron-core. `spawn`'s ProfileResolver is an injected DI seam, never a flywheel import in toron.
4. **One backend trait** after P1.
5. **Resonate is the only execution substrate.** Cron manager = durable-sleep loop.
6. **Backward compat.** `triage.yaml`, the ADR-0004 suite, AND the captain's live flywheel `workflows`/`pipeline`/`recipes` runs must pass at every phase boundary.
7. `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Tokio, rmcp, Schnorr identity, NIP-17 E2E — all preserved.

## The phasing (this epic's children, in execution order)
- **P0 — Failure propagation** (PREREQUISITE: blocks P4, P5). ActionRunner Result<()>→Result<Value>; on_error:fail_run; kind-46012 status=failed.
- **P1 — Backend trait unification.** ONE trait; migrate ~20 &mut dyn call sites.

title: Mention coalescing: batch N @mentions to one assignee into 1 job (Buzz queue.rs pattern)
description:
# Mention coalescing in dispatch.rs (Buzz buzz-acp queue.rs pattern)

## Problem
toron's dispatch_job creates one kind-43001 per @mention. An @mention burst to one agent
= N separate prompts, burning context. Buzz's buzz-acp (queue.rs, 2565 LOC) batches N
queued events per channel into ONE session/prompt. This is the single highest-leverage
agent-automation efficiency win from the Buzz study.

## What
Add a coalescing layer in crates/toron-workflow/src/dispatch.rs:
- collect @mentions within a short window (e.g. 2s, configurable) per assignee
- emit ONE coalesced job (kind-43001 with combined spec, or one session/prompt-equivalent)
  instead of N
- preserve ordering; dedup identical mentions within the window

## Buzz reference
crates/buzz-acp/src/queue.rs — per-channel event queue, batching, dedup. "At most one
prompt is in-flight per channel. Queued events are batched into a single prompt sent via
session/prompt over ACP."

## Acceptance
- N @mentions to one assignee within window → 1 dispatched job
- mentions outside window → separate jobs (no infinite coalesce)
- SC-12 (burst backpressure) still passes
- new test: burst-coalesce count assertion
- no context-window regression (measure: 20 mentions → 1 prompt, not 20)

## Files
crates/toron-workflow/src/dispatch.rs, crates/toron-workflow/src/jobs.rs

## governed-by
ADR-0003 §Phase 2 (Buzz adopt: @mention-as-dispatch); study doc
docs/notes/2026-08-07-buzz-agentmail-comparison.md item L2/1
close_reason: Ship 1/5 of ADR-0004. Shipped: crates/toron-workflow/src/coalesce.rs (MentionCoalescer). 11 unit tests pass. Per-assignee windows (default 2s, env TORON_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS), immediate-flush sub-window (500ms, env TORON_COALESCE_SUBWINDOW_MS) so lone mentions dispatch fast, hard cap (64) prevents infinite coalesce, dedup identical (parent,spec), order preserved. Pure + sync + allocation-only — no I/O, no event-building; callers flush buffers and build kind-43001 from Coalesced.merged_spec(). SC-12 backpressure still green. cargo test --workspace green. clippy --workspace -D warnings clean. verify-gates pass. governed-by: ADR-0004 Ship 1.

# F6 — renew_file_reservations extended to 2x instead of +extend

## Evidence (real-e2e opencode probe, 2026-08-06)
renew advanced expires_ts_us from 1786022764000000 to 3572045556000000 (2x). Root cause: reservations.rs renew treated the absolute epoch expires_ts_us as a RELATIVE duration and re-added to now, double-counting elapsed time.

## Fix (applied)
new_expiry = old_abs_expiry + extend_secs (absolute), stored as relative TTL (new_abs - now) so NIP-40 expiration = now + ttl lands at the right absolute time. Test test_renew_and_release green.

description:
# Workstream P2.1: toron-workflow Resonate-backed + @mention + jobs 43001–43006

## Ship order #1 (captain) — highest automation leverage

## toron-workflow crate
YAML workflows channel/project-scoped:
### Triggers
message_posted, reaction_added, reservation_acquired/released, agent_state_changed, schedule, webhook
### Actions
send_message, send_dm, react, dispatch_job, call_webhook, request_approval, delay
### Events
Each run/step/approval = kind 46001–46012 **and** Resonate durable promise
### Crash survival
request_approval suspends, **survives process crash**, resumes on approval (Buzz WF-08 fix)
### delay
Resonate durable sleep unbounded (vs Buzz 270s cap)
### dispatch_job (A7)

title: P11.1 Reactive ingress (bus to workflow triggers)
description:
# What
Wire bus events to workflow triggers so reactive workflows actually fire. Foundational: the coalition detector (P11.3) and cascade/handoff (SC-10) cannot run without it. Closes the ADR-0007 trigger-ingress gap (message_posted closed by construction; reservation_acquired/released uncertain).

A persistent bus subscriber (toron-cli daemon / flywheel) evaluates incoming events through trigger_filter (loop-prevention already exists) and invokes WorkflowEngine::invoke for matching triggered workflows.

# Blast radius
toron-workflow/src/trigger_filter.rs (the ingress loop wiring); toron-cli/src (the bus subscriber that drives it) OR flywheel/src (if flywheel owns the subscriber). Verify which process owns the live subscriber. No schema change (triggers already declared); this is the WIRING, not the schema.

# Verification gate
A workflow with trigger reservation_acquired fires when a 30031 is acquired (a test acquires + the workflow run starts); message_posted fires on a user-authored message (NOT on workflow-emitted — loop-prevention holds); reaction_added / reservation_released likewise. The loop-prevention gate (workflow-emitted tag) still rejects re-triggers.

# Dependency
After ADR-0010 P10.1 (the real runner — triggered workflows need to actually execute). See ADR-0011 Spec 3 + P11.1.
close_reason:
P11.1 reactive ingress wired. Live subscriber verified: the toron-mcp serve host owns it (toron-cli daemon is lifecycle-only, no bus - no CLI change needed).

WHAT LANDED:
(a) toron-workflow trigger_filter.rs: the ingress EVALUATION layer - matches_trigger (kind-level + reservation acquired/released DISAMBIGUATION via released/revoked marker + reservation project/path scoping + optional message channel/project + reaction emoji), trigger_payload (id/sender/content/kind/created_at/tags/project/channel/importance + reservation status field), trigger_run_id (engine idempotency key). Loop-prevention filter untouched.
(b) THE REAL GAP (found via TDD): the raw-bus run_trigger_loop subscribed with Filter::new() = a GLOBAL subscription - the A3 access gate excludes every project-scoped event from global subs, so reservation (30031) and reaction (7) events NEVER reached the loop; it was dead code with zero production call sites. Fixed with a TRUSTED ingress subscription: Bus::subscribe_trusted (A3 global-gate bypass; InProcessBus + RelayBus + test-double impls; trusted sub only for the mailbox's own internal consumers) + run_trigger_loop now subscribes trusted.
(c) toron-mcp server.rs: spawn_trigger_loop (raw-bus reactive loop) armed ALONGSIDE spawn_mail_trigger_loop in the serve path - reservation_acquired/released + reaction_added go live in production.

GATES (all GREEN): workflow(trigger=reservation_acquired) fires when a 30031 acquired; reservation_released fires on release marker ONLY (not on acquire); reaction_added on kind-7; message_posted on user kind-14; stamped (workflow-emitted) kind-14 does NOT re-trigger (loop prevention end-to-end).

EVIDENCE: toron-workflow 132P/0F (+5 new trigger_filter tests); toron-mcp 37P+5P+7P+1P (+host-level bus_trigger_loop gate test); toron-core 363P/0F (+subscribe_trusted test); e2e all green; clippy clean on touched files (only pre-existing config/mod.rs debt).

title: P11.2 request-release negotiation + soft-conflict check + intent TTL
description:
# What
The collab floor + the load-bearing mechanism. Two coupled changes:

(a) request-release negotiation: a typed message (Crew A asks B to release/defer a held reservation) + an escalation tier (no response within a window escalates to a kind-14 DM to the captain). Replaces today binary (voluntary-release | operator force-release) with a negotiation ladder. Force-release stays the operator last resort.

(b) the soft-conflict check + intent state: extend check_file_reservation_conflicts so a status:intent 30031 is a SOFT conflict (acquire against an intent = freeze + propose, NOT hard-block); a held reservation stays a HARD conflict (block as today). Plus intent TTL + must-convert (an intent auto-expires ~5min unless it converts to held).

# Why load-bearing
Without the soft-conflict check, soft-default acquire beats the reactive detector (a fast acquirer holds before the detector proposes) and the intent layer degrades to request-release. The soft-conflict check is the mechanism that makes intent-based coordination actually work. The atomic HARD floor is NEVER removed.

# Blast radius
toron-core/src/mailbox/reservations.rs (status field on 30031 + soft-conflict branch in the check + TTL/expiry); toron-mcp/src (the request-release tool surface, if MCP) or flywheel CLI (the negotiation commands). No new Nostr kind (30031 status extension).

# Verification gate
Acquiring a path against a declared in-TTL intent returns a SOFT conflict (freeze+propose), NOT a hard block; acquiring against a held reservation hard-blocks (unchanged); acquiring with no conflict succeeds immediately (no latency). An intent expires after TTL if not converted to held. A request-release message escalates to a captain DM after the tier window.

# Dependency
After P11.1 (reactive ingress — the detector workflow that consumes the soft-conflict freeze fires via ingress). See ADR-0011 Spec 2, 4, 6 + P11.2.
close_reason:
P11.2 complete. Landed in toron-core/src/mailbox/reservations.rs + additive MCP outputs (no new tools, no arg changes — ADR-0011 forbidden zone respected).

IMPLEMENTED:
- 30031 status state machine (Held|Intent|Released|Revoked); status-less = held (backward compat). resolved_leases = single replay feeding held view / intent board / conflict view.
- declare_intent() publishes status:intent + NIP-40 (default INTENT_TTL_SECS=300); active_intents() = in-TTL board; must-convert: own acquire supersedes intent at same (kind,d) -> held.
- conflict_view splits HARD (held exclusive, other) vs SOFT (in-TTL intent, other). Acquire vs intent = freeze (granted empty, soft_conflicts, NOT hard block); held hard-blocks unchanged; clear acquire immediate. check_file_reservation_conflicts reports soft_conflicts + has_soft_conflicts (conflict_free stays hard-only contract).
- Request-release ladder: request_release (typed kind-14 rumor, toron-kind=request-release, ask/reservation-id/e-refs, importance high, ack_required; validates exists/held/holder/self) -> respond_request_release (toron-kind=request-release-response + decision tag, NIP-10 reply ref; only addressed holder can respond — p-tag gate) -> request_release_status (Pending|Responded latest-wins|EscalationDue|Unknown) -> escalate_request_release (kind-14 DM to captain=operator, toron-kind=request-release-escalation, importance high; operator-key gated). Force-release untouched.

EVIDENCE:
- 9 new gate tests in reservations.rs: declare+board, soft-not-hard acquire, held hard-blocks unchanged, clear acquire immediate, TTL expiry unblocks acquire, must-convert, tiered report, request-release roundtrip+validations, status Pending->EscalationDue->captain DM, response resolution (incl. deferred round-trip + third-party denied), operator gate.
- toron-core 362P/0F/1I; toron-mcp 36P+5P+7P+1P; e2e all green; clippy -D warnings clean on touched files (pre-existing config/mod.rs doc-lint debt, not my lane).
- MCP: AcquireResult/ConflictReport gain additive soft_conflicts/has_soft_conflicts keys (ToJson + Out schema).

title: P11.3a Coalition lifecycle + CLI (steer surface, manual collab)
description:
# What (RESCOPED from the original P11.3 — detector+proposer split out to P11.3b)
The coalition object + steer surface + manual collab. Valuable WITHOUT the auto-detector: crews declare intents + use P11.2's request-release negotiation manually.

- Coalition = NIP-29 channel (intent board + shared thread) + workflow run (goal driver). Ephemeral, pane-crew-only (headless cron separate).
- 30031 status:intent declaration surface: a crew declares an intent (status:intent, with TTL from P11.2) into the coalition channel (the intent board).
- Formation: captain-formed (flywheel coalition form GOAL --crews SQUAD) — creates the channel + starts the goal run. Auto-coalesce is P11.3b.
- Manual collab: on a soft-conflict (P11.2's check freezes the acquirer), the crews use request-release negotiation (P11.2) to resolve — NO auto-proposer yet (that is P11.3b). This is the un-automated baseline.
- Disband: beads-closed primary | auto-fallback (workflow-run terminal / timeout). Channel closes + run ends; held reservations released.
- CLI: flywheel coalition {form, status, disband}.

# Blast radius
flywheel/src/coalition.rs NEW (lifecycle + channel/run binding + status/disband); flywheel/src/main.rs (CoalitionCmd). Reuses P11.2 (soft-conflict freeze + negotiation). NO detector workflow here (that is P11.3b). toron-workflow unchanged (the goal run is an authored workflow).

# Verification gate
flywheel coalition form <goal> --crews <squad> creates a NIP-29 channel + starts the goal run; a crew declares status:intent into the board (visible in coalition status); a second crew acquiring the same path hits P11.2's soft-conflict FREEZE; the two resolve via P11.2 request-release negotiation (manually, no auto-proposal); beads-closed disbands the coalition (channel closes). Auto-detection (P11.3b) is NOT exercised here.

# Dependency
After P11.2 (soft-conflict freeze + negotiation). NOT dependent on P11.1 ingress (manual coordination needs no workflow triggers). See ADR-0011 Spec 1.

title: P11.3b Detector + tiered proposer + auto-coalesce
description:
# What (SPLIT OUT of the original P11.3 — the automation layer)
The auto-detector + tiered proposer + auto-coalesce. Automates the overlap detection + split proposal that P11.3a's manual collab does by hand.

- Detector: a workflow-as-reaction on reservation_acquired with status=intent (fires via P11.1 ingress). Reads the coalition intent board; detects overlaps.
- Tiered proposer: deterministic rules first (split by directory boundary / bead-dependency; sequence by dep; merge if same bead). Escalate to an LLM planner ONLY if a crew rejects the rule-split. The LLM arm is a headless planner run (ADR-0010 P10.1).
- Auto-coalesce: when the detector finds an overlap between two UNAFFILIATED crews (not already in a coalition) on non-trivial source overlap (shared source dir, NOT README/config/docs), it auto-forms an ad-hoc coalition + proposes the split.
- Wires into P11.3a: the soft-conflict freeze (P11.2) now triggers the detector workflow (which proposes) instead of requiring manual negotiation. Manual negotiation (P11.2) remains the dispute backstop when a proposal is rejected.

# Blast radius
flywheel/src/intent.rs NEW (intent board read + tiered proposer rules); flywheel/src/main.rs (detector workflow wiring + auto-coalesce hook on the soft-conflict path); the detector IS an authored workflow YAML (no engine change). A path-classification rule for non-trivial-source (source vs doc/config) — an ignore-list/suffix check.

# Verification gate
Two crews (in or outside a coalition) declare overlapping intents on a source dir; the detector fires (via P11.1 ingress) + proposes a rule-split (dir/dependency); rejecting it fires the LLM planner; agreeing converts both to held (non-overlapping). Two crews overlapping on a README/config do NOT auto-coalesce. The proposal is wired into the P11.2 soft-conflict freeze path (freeze -> detector proposes, not manual-only).

# Dependency
After P11.3a (coalition context + intent board) + P11.1 (ingress — the detector is a workflow-as-reaction). See ADR-0011 Spec 3.

title: P10.3 Pane runner + crew (interactive; complex)
description:
# What
Real PANE execution for interactive workflows (you watch). Crew pre-spawn + dispatch via herdr.

- Real pane ActionRunner ("workflow run --execute --mode pane"): spawn/dispatch_job shell to "flywheel __send" (the loop's proven confirmed-send path); pre-spawn the crew before invoke.
- Crew pre-spawn: CrewPlan -> profile::resolve -> cmd_spawn -> agent_start(kind, AGENT_ARG=[--model..]). Engine then dispatches to the existing crew (ProfileResolver maps @role -> running pane).
- Lifecycle: ephemeral default (reap at run end) + --reuse WORKSPACE + --retain. herdr owns panes -> survive flywheel crash; re-bind on resume; orphans via --retire-orphans.
- Crew registry: extend save_spawn_registry (state.rs) with a PROFILE column -> resolve @planner -> name -> pane.
- Behavior preamble prepend on pane dispatch too (same runner path as headless).

# Blast radius
flywheel/src/main.rs (RealRunner pane path + --reuse/--retain flags + pre-spawn wiring); flywheel/src/crew.rs (CrewPlan -> spawn); flywheel/src/state.rs (spawn-registry profile column). Reuses the loop __send leaf (no new dispatch code).

# Verification gate
"flywheel workflow run CREW-WF --execute" (a workflow with crew {planner:1, coder:1}) spawns 2 real herdr panes (visible in flywheel list), dispatches each step with the profile behavior preamble prepended (verified via agent_read of first lines), and --reuse/--retain behave. No-op default unchanged.

# Why later (not first)
Refactors the ALREADY-WORKING interactive path (flywheel loop runs swarms today). Net-new headless value (P10.1) ships first; this is the bigger, riskier change.

title: P10.1 Headless execution slice (real runner, simplest observable value)
description:
# What
The smallest end-to-end real-execution slice. A workflow actually RUNS headlessly and logs.

- New hidden leaf flywheel __run-headless PROFILE PROMPT [--model X] [--json]: resolve profile to harness, run "harness -p --mode=json PROMPT", capture JSON stdout, write ~/.local/state/flywheel/runs/RUN_ID.jsonl.
- Real ActionRunner (HEADLESS path only): "workflow run --execute --mode headless" dispatches each step via __run-headless. await:true = block on subprocess + capture JSON into steps.NAME; await:false = detached + log-when-done.
- Behavior-preamble prepend IN THE RUNNER (leaves stay dumb): resolve the step profile, read Profile.behavior, construct PREAMBLE + step prompt before calling the leaf.
- Run-log reader: "flywheel runs show ID" reads headless logs (full response); "digest" aggregates.

# Blast radius
flywheel/src/main.rs (__run-headless leaf + WorkflowCmd::Run gains --execute/--mode + RealRunner headless path); flywheel/src/headless.rs NEW (harness -p adapter per omp/opencode/pi/grok); flywheel/src/run_log.rs NEW (runs/ID.jsonl write+read). No toron-workflow change. No herdr (headless = subprocess only).

# Verification gate
"flywheel workflow run plan --execute --mode headless --inputs {goal:decompose X}" runs the planner headlessly, writes runs/RUN_ID.jsonl with {response, tokens_in, tokens_out, status, model, duration_ms}, and "flywheel runs show RUN_ID" prints the full response. No-op default (workflow run without --execute) unchanged.

# Why first
Headless is the SIMPLEST real execution (no herdr workspace/crew/promise binding) and serves the net-new cron capability. Ships observable value before the complex pane runner (which refactors the already-working loop).

title: Replace .expect() panics in mailbox send/messaging path with typed errors
description:
# F1 — .expect() panics in messaging send path (partial-delivery + process-crash hazard)

## Evidence of defect (v1.0.0 @ fc96a23)
`crates/toron-core/src/mailbox/messaging.rs` has **35 `.expect()` calls** in the hot path:
- `gift_wrap::gift_wrap(...).await.expect("wrap to/cc")` — panics mid-send on a single wrap failure
- `.expect("wrap bcc")` — same, in the bcc variant loop
- `.expect("wrap receipt")`, `.expect("register")`, `.expect("connect")`, `.expect("bus")`, `.expect("load key")`, `.expect("toron-kind tag")`, `.expect("p tag")` (x3), `.expect("subject tag")`, `.expect("importance tag")`, `.expect("ack-required tag")`, `.expect("sender-token tag")`

## Soundness gap
- **Progress**: a single transient gift-wrap/crypto/tag-parse failure panics the whole process. N recipients → up to N+1 panic sites. Partial delivery already happened for prior recipients (no rollback) AND the caller gets no Result.
- **Foot-gun**: medium-ease-of-misuse (any future caller assumes send_message returns Result; it panics instead), silent-on-partial (delivered recipients are not reported on panic).
- **Inhabitance**: the function signature returns `Result<SendResult>` but the Ok path is unreachable on wrap failure — the type lies.

## Minimum acceptable fix (narrowest truthful)
Replace every `.expect("...")` in messaging.rs with `?` (propagate via `anyhow`/`thiserror`). Add a new `MessagingError` enum with variants: `WrapFailure`, `TagBuild`, `PublishFailure`. The ADR's 'unknown recipient aborts whole send (no partial delivery)' contract is preserved by failing BEFORE any wrap is published (the recipient-resolution step already does this) — wraps after that point can fail without violating the contract, just return Err with the partial `deliveries` so far in a structured error.

## Do NOT broaden into
- A retry/backoff layer (separate concern).
- An idempotent-send redesign (out of scope).
- Replacing expect() across the whole codebase (only the messaging hot path matters here).

## Remediation posture
Narrow. Pure error-propagation replacement, no architectural change. ~35 1-line edits + a typed error enum + tests asserting a forced wrap failure returns Err (not panic).
close_reason: FIXED: replaced 4 gift-wrap/toron-kind .expect() panics in messaging send/receipt hot path with ? propagation (map_err with recipient-named context). The 4 user-input tag expects (subject/importance/ack-required/sender-token) made tolerant (silently dropped on invalid input — matches AM-Rust). The 2 static p-tag expects (npub hex + role literal — infallible) kept with narrowed justifications. cargo test -p toron-core messaging: 6/6 pass. clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

# Declare outputSchema on MCP tools (ADR-0003 rev7 L33 SEP-2106 structured outputs)

## Problem
ADR-0003 rev7 (2026-08-05) L33 lists "**structured outputs (SEP-2106)**" as an adopted efficiency
lever, and L31 says schemars-derived `outputSchema` is the conformance source. Reality: 0/38 toron
tools declare `outputSchema`. The lever is aspirational, not shipped.

## Why it matters
- outputSchema lets clients (incl. pi's adapter) parse tool results into typed shapes without
  heuristics — the same parity contract that governs inputSchema should govern outputs.
- Without it, toron's response shapes are the "real-e2e probe divergences" catalogued in bd-96a
  (npub vs id, wrap-id vs numeric delivery id, released vs released_at, etc.) — undocumented at the
  schema layer, discovered only by probe.

## Scope
Declare outputSchema on the 38 tools. Large effort — each tool's return type needs a schemars-derived
struct. Prioritize by probe-divergence surface:
1. identity cluster (whois, list_agents, register_agent, create_agent_identity) — biggest divergence
2. messaging cluster (send_message, reply_message, fetch_inbox) — payload shape divergence
3. reservations/slots (release_*, renew_*) — missing released_at-style fields
4. the rest

## Acceptance
- outputSchema present on all 38 tools
- cargo test --workspace green
- bd-96a / bd-3mp (parity catalog) reference the schemas instead of free-text divergence notes

## Files
crates/toron-mcp/src/tools.rs (struct-per-return-type), possibly a new responses.rs

## governed-by
ADR-0003 rev7 L31, L33

## Depends on
bd-96a (parity shape catalog — informs the schema shapes)

# toron doctor reconstruct (Agent Mail A1)

## Problem
toron has sc14a_dr_rebuild test proving rebuild-from-Git works, but no operator CLI.
Agent Mail ships `am doctor reconstruct`: capture forensic bundle, quarantine bad DB,
rebuild fresh SQLite from Git archive, merge into place. The capability exists in toron;
the operator surface doesn't.

## What
- `toron doctor reconstruct` — wraps existing crates/toron-core/src/index/rebuild.rs
- capture forensic bundle (SQLite dump + config) before mutating
- quarantine bad DB (.db.quarantined-<ts>), rebuild fresh from Git archive
- merge into place atomically
- exit codes: 0 ok, 1 rebuild-failed (quarantined DB preserved), 3 doctor-diagnostic

## Acceptance
- `toron doctor reconstruct` on a corrupted SQLite → fresh working DB from Git
- forensic bundle preserved
- sc14a_dr_rebuild logic reused (not duplicated)
- new e2e: corrupt DB → reconstruct → state consistent

## Files
crates/toron-cli/src/operator.rs (or new doctor.rs), crates/toron-core/src/index/rebuild.rs

## governed-by
ADR-0003 §DR (G11); study doc docs/notes/2026-08-07-buzz-agentmail-comparison.md item A1/2
close_reason: Ship 3/5 of ADR-0004. Shipped: toron doctor reconstruct. Reuses proven rebuild_index_from_git (sc14a_dr_rebuild parity proof). New: toron-core inspect_index(path)->(exists,integrity_ok,rows) + build_fresh_index(path,archive)->(rebuilt,rows) [WAL-checkpointed for atomic rename]. CLI: DoctorArgs gains #[command(subcommand)] DoctorCmd::Reconstruct(DoctorReconstructArgs{dry_run,project,data_dir}). Flow per project: integrity+row pre-check → Healthy(skip) OR forensic bundle (move index.sqlite{,-wal,-shm}.orig + manifest.json into doctor-forensic-{ts}/) → build fresh at index.sqlite.new (connect+migrate+rebuild+wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE) → convergence verify (rows==rebuilt==archive_count) → drop orphaned -wal/-shm → atomic POSIX rename .new->index.sqlite. Exit codes via pure classify_exit(ReconstructExit{Ok,Failed,Diagnostic}): 0 ok · 1 failed(quarantine preserved) · 3 diagnostic(no data dir / no project archives). Data-dir resolution: --data-dir > TORON_DATA_DIR > config data_dir. WAL gotcha: schema::connect forces WAL mode; renamed main file orphans -wal (reads malformed) — fixed by checkpoint(TRUNCATE) + drop siblings. 7 tests: restore-deleted, healthy-noop, drift-quarantine, dry-run, classify_exit mapping, no-data-dir→3, success→0. CLI smoke: doctor reconstruct --help + direct binary exit 3 confirmed. cargo test --workspace green (34 bins), clippy --workspace -D warnings clean, verify-gates pass. governed-by: ADR-0004 Ship 3. NOTE: same engine-wiring gap as Ships 1/2/4 — the daemon's demo_mailbox uses a temp data_dir, not a persistent project layout; reconstruct operates on an explicit --data-dir. When the daemon gains a persistent data_dir, reconstruct targets it directly.

title: ADR-0003 Phase 1: AM-Rust parity Nostr mailbox (v1)
description:
# Epic: ADR-0003 Phase 1 — AM-Rust parity Nostr mailbox (v1 ship target)

## Background
`toron` v0.1.0 was built on asupersync + mDNS/PSK/WS-QUIC hub (ADR-0001/0002). ADR-0003 (accepted 2026-08-04, rev 6) pivots to:
- **Protocol:** Nostr (signed events + NIP-17 DMs)
- **Runtime:** Tokio (captain override of asupersync)
- **Role:** mailbox with **100% behavioral parity** to `mcp_agent_mail_rust` (AM-Rust) — 38 MCP tools / 9 clusters, 25 resources, storage layout, safety invariants, pre-commit guard, CLI robot mode + metrics
- **Topology:** Decision 1A (InProcessBus default) + 2B (nostr-sdk/Tokio) + 3A (flywheel embeds toron in-process)

## Goals / why this serves the project
Agents coordinate through durable, signed, relay/bus-delivered mail instead of shared filesystem state or a single SQLite process. Nostr adds: (1) cryptographic identity, (2) real-time pub/sub, (3) federation opt-in, (4) metadata-hiding private mail (NIP-17/59). Local-first preserved via InProcessBus + Git + SQLite.

## Non-negotiable parity contract
- Behavioral parity = tool surface + resources + storage + invariants (NOT runtime parity — asupersync waived)
- Conformance scope = response schema + filter/importance/thread/date semantics + tokenizer (`porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, `prefix='2 3'`) — NOT exact Search-V3 ranking
- Fixtures re-derived first-party (AM-Rust is `LicenseRef-MIT-Rider` — no vendoring)
- Kind registry FROZEN (30010–30014, 30031, 30032, Buzz job 43001–43006, etc.) — renumber requires new ADR revision

## Phase 1 OUT of scope (Phase 2+)
- toron-workflow / @mention dispatch / job lifecycle automation
- NIP-29 channels
- Ephemeral presence + persona packs
- TUI (ratatui 16-screen)
- Blossom/NIP-96 federation for blobs
- NIP-46 remote signer (Phase 1.5 option)
- NIP-05/39 (Phase 3 / A9)

## Architecture (concrete)
Layers in `toron-core`: Nostr → Bus → Local Projection (SQLite+Git) → Mailbox Core → Backend trait.
`toron-mcp` = 38 tools MCP (stdio/HTTP). `toron-cli` = daemon + robot CLI.
flywheel embeds toron-core+toron-mcp; agent↔agent path has no orchestrator in the loop.

## Success = all Phase-1 verification checkboxes in ADR-0003 Implementation Plan §Verification
## Source of truth
docs/decisions/0003-nostr-mailbox-fabric.md (rev 6). Beads must be self-contained; this epic anchors the tree.

title: Bus: InProcessBus + pipeline (RelayBus optional/federation)
description:
# Workstream: Bus trait — InProcessBus + RelayBus

## Decision 1A
Default = InProcessBus (Tokio broadcast + SQLite event store). RelayBus for standalone daemon / federation. Events are **wire-identical** — serialize any InProcessBus event and a real relay accepts it unchanged.

## Critical framing
- InProcessBus is NOT a NIP-01-interoperable relay (no external client can REQ it)
- It has relay-identical **event semantics** + same validation pipeline
- RelayBus speaks full NIP-01 frames (EVENT/REQ/OK/EOSE)

## Buzz relay pipeline (adopt exactly)
verify → auth → dedup-insert (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) → fan-out (global subs excluded from channel/project-scoped events) → search-index (bounded worker) → audit (async) → workflow-trigger (async; excludes workflow/gift-wrap kinds). Client OK at pipeline end.

## Tagging (A3)
- InProcessBus: `["t", project-slug]` cheap filter
- Relay-crossing kinds ALSO carry NIP-32: `["L","toron"]` + `["l", project-slug, "toron"]` (dual-emit preferred)
- Gift-wrapped DMs (14/15/ack) carry **NEITHER** #t nor NIP-32 (metadata-hiding)

## Federation (Phase 1 policy NEW-D3)
- Default relay list **empty** (opt-in; zero egress)
- Only NIP-17 gift wraps may cross external relays in Phase 1
- Reservations/manifests/channels NOT federated until owned relay
- Public-relay hardening (never silent): NIP-42 AUTH + NIP-13 POW + allowlist (A4)

## TTL
Gift-wrap envelopes TTL 90 days (NIP-40 expiration, configurable). Git archive permanent.

## Ordering note (G7)
Bus envelope order = lex `(created_at, event_id)` for non-wrapped storage only. Mail timeline uses rumor timestamps after unwrap — separate projection concern.

comments.text:
## InProcessBus framing

Not a real NIP-01 relay. External clients cannot REQ it. Events are still wire-identical so RelayBus and federation do not need a second event type. Pipeline order matches Buzz: verify→auth→dedup→access-gated fanout→search→audit→workflow-trigger.

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — RELIABILITY (prevents silent data loss):

The "Tokio broadcast (or equivalent)" line needs a hard rule. `tokio::sync::broadcast` DROPS the oldest messages for laggy receivers (`Receiver::lagged`). That is unacceptable for the **projection subscriber** (bd-led.4.4), which must process EVERY event to keep SQLite + Git in sync — a dropped broadcast = a missing projected message = silent data loss.

Rule: the DURABLE subscribers (projection, archive) MUST use a lossless channel — per-subscriber `mpsc`, or a store-cursor + notify model backed by the SQLite event store (subscribe from a monotonic event-id cursor; notify-on-insert). `broadcast` is acceptable ONLY for loss-tolerant / ephemeral consumers (presence, debug streams).

Reconcile-on-lag (catch up from the event store by event-id cursor when a notification is missed) is the alternative if broadcast is kept for liveness. Don't ship the durable projection on a dropping channel.

Bus is dumb. Projection drops wraps that violate recipient policy before index/Git.

Bus = current replaceable state; Git = full transition history for reservations/slots.

- **bcc:** variant rumor listing to+cc+that_bcc only (true BCC; bcc cannot see other bccs)

- thread reply → NIP-10 `["e", root, relay, "reply"]`
- Unknown recipient **aborts whole send** (no partial delivery)

## Acks / reads (G8)
- NOT public replaceable events
- NIP-17 gift-wrapped kind-14 to original sender only
- tags: `toron-kind` = `ack`|`read` + NIP-10 `e` referencing original (no `d` on kind 14)
- `acknowledge_message` **idempotent** (second call returns stored ts)

## Ordering
fetch_inbox uses projection mail timeline (rumor time), never envelope time (G7)

## Acceptance tests (must all pass, detailed logs)
1. N recipients → N kind-1059 wraps; each unwraps to same kind-14 rumor content
2. BCC recipient unwrap lists to+cc+self, **not** other bccs
3. Non-recipient cannot unwrap any wrap
4. Ack only visible to original sender's projection
5. Idempotent ack returns same timestamp
6. Real-time: subscribed local agent receives via bus push (no poll) — integration with bus
7. `to=["Unknown"]` fails fast pre-wrap

## Why better than AM-Rust
E2E gift-wrap + true BCC + private acks (parity superiority table).

description:
# Task: File reservation cluster (5 tools) + force-release G5 A1

## Tools

(Exact names from catalog `bd-0qg`.)

## Wire
- kind-30031 addressable; `d`=`project:path-glob`; NIP-40 expiration=TTL
- Conflict detection: local **symmetric** fnmatch both ways (`src/**` ↔ `src/lib.rs`)

## Force-release (G5 A1) — DO NOT USE CROSS-KEY NIP-09
NIP-09 is author-only. Operator kind-5 cannot delete agent reservation.
NIP-33 addressable dedup is per `(kind,pubkey,d)` — operator cannot supersede agent event on relay.

### Normative mechanism
1. Validate staleness heuristic (agent inactive beyond threshold — same as AM-Rust)
2. Operator signs kind-30031 with `status:revoked` + `e`/`a` → target lease
3. **Projection key-priority: operator > agent** for given `(kind,d)` — all nodes identical
4. NIP-09 only optional cleanup hint / agent own-deletes
5. Notify previous holder via NIP-17 with heuristic summary
6. Git audit transition record (G13 history)

## Acceptance tests
1. Symmetric conflict both directions
2. TTL expiry clears active lease
3. Force-release: projection shows revoked **with both agent lease + operator revoke events present**
4. No dependence on NIP-09 delete succeeding
5. Previous holder receives NIP-17 notify
6. Git has acquired→revoked transition history
7. broadcast=true / wrong-surface denied at tool layer (cross-check invariants bead)

## Depends on
Projection unwrap, addressable priority (`bd-toh`), operator keys, dual-emit tags.

description:
# Task: toron-mcp server skeleton (rmcp, spec 2026-07-28)

## What
Build the MCP server on **rmcp** (NOT fastmcp-rust — asupersync conflict). Two transports from one `ServerHandler` impl:

1. **stdio** (feature `transport-io`) — for `toron serve --mcp-stdio` and as a child-process server agents spawn.
2. **Streamable HTTP** (feature `transport-streamable-http-server`) — `StreamableHttpService` is a Tower service; mount it on toron's axum router at `/mcp`. This is the current spec transport; legacy 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE is a deliberate rmcp non-goal (do NOT build it). Enable **SEP-2567 stateless mode** for the daemon/federation path (horizontally scalable, no session affinity).

## ServerHandler
- `get_info()`: `ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().enable_resources().enable_resources_subscribe().enable_tool_list_changed().enable_logging().build()`; server name `toron`, version from Cargo.
- Protocol negotiation: prefer `ProtocolVersion::V_2026_07_28`; rmcp auto-falls-back to `V_2025_11_25`.
- Lifecycle: `serve()` (legacy initialize) for stdio; `serve_with_lifecycle(Discover)` for HTTP clients that prefer it.

## Foundation for 7.2 / 7.3
- ServerHandler holds an `Arc<Mailbox>` (toron-core). 7.2 adds `#[tool]` methods; 7.3 adds `#[resource]` + subscriptions.
- Macros (`#[tool_router]`, `#[tool_handler]`) auto-wire capability flags.

## Acceptance
- `toron serve --mcp-stdio` answers `initialize`/`list_tools` (empty) over stdio.
- `toron serve --mcp-http 127.0.0.1:8000` mounts `StreamableHttpService` on axum; an rmcp client (`transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest`) completes `initialize`.
- Negotiated protocol reports `2026-07-28` against a current client.
- No fastmcp / asupersync in the server path.

CLI toron serve --mcp-stdio/--mcp-http. Acceptance proven: live binary smoke negotiate 2026-07-28 over both transports, tools/list empty, exit 0; acceptance.rs tests 2/2; workspace check/test/clippy(-D warnings)/fmt all green; rg fastmcp/asupersync empty. Features: transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest added for tests.

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05) — MATERIAL DEPENDENCY FIX:

`fastmcp-rust` (Dicklesworthstone/fastmcp_rust — the crate currently named in bd-led.1.2 + ADR-0003 §Dependencies) is built on `asupersync`. That is the exact runtime ADR-0003 DROPS (captain Tokio override), and whose removal is a hard CI gate (`rg asupersync` zero hits across toron + flywheel). Pulling fastmcp-rust into toron re-introduces asupersync transitively and mixes two async runtimes in one process (tokio + asupersync) — a known footgun, and a direct violation of the ADR's runtime-waiver intent.

USE THE OFFICIAL `rmcp` CRATE instead — `modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk`, Tokio-native, ships `#[tool]`/`#[resource]`/`#[prompt]` macros via `rmcp-macros`. Matches the mandate; sufficient for 38 tools + 25 resources. Fallback if rmcp proves too minimal for the surface: hand-roll MCP JSON-RPC over stdio/axum (the protocol is simple) — still preferable to fastmcp-rust's runtime conflict.

Action for this bead: build the stdio + HTTP/axum MCP skeleton on `rmcp`. Action for bd-led.1.2: declare `rmcp` + `rmcp-macros`, drop `fastmcp-rust 0.3.x`. ADR-0003 §Dependencies + §Migration need a corrigendum (fastmcp-rust → rmcp) — flagged to captain; not silently editing the accepted/frozen ADR here.

title: Wire 38 tools 1:1 AM-Rust names/args/returns
description:
# Task: Wire 38 AM-Rust tools on rmcp (macros + schemars; spec 2026-07-28)

## Approach — macro-driven, schema-by-derive (the efficiency win)
Use rmcp `#[tool]` + `#[tool_router]` (or `#[tool_router(server_handler)]`) on the Mailbox impl. Each of the 38 tools = one method whose params struct and return struct derive `serde::{Serialize,Deserialize}` + `schemars::JsonSchema`. rmcp auto-generates `inputSchema` + `outputSchema` (JSON Schema 2020-12) — **NO hand-rolled schemas**.

## Conformance source = the derived schemas
The schemars-derived inputSchema/outputSchema ARE the golden fixture for the 38-tool schema conformance (bd-77u.1). Snapshot them at compile time (from the rmcp-reported `list_tools` output); no need to run each tool to record its shape. AM-Rust arg names / return shapes map 1:1 to the derive field names/types — **parity-by-construction**.

## Structured outputs (SEP-2106)
Return structs carry `outputSchema` + populated `structuredContent`. outputSchema may be any JSON type. Tools that today return JSON blobs (search results, thread summaries, inbox lists) get typed return structs.

## Tool annotations (2026-07-28)
Annotate for host gating (annotations are untrusted per spec but useful): `destructive=true` for `force_release_file_reservation`, `file_reservation_paths(exclusive)`, `acquire_build_slot(exclusive)`, `install_precommit_guard`; `read-only` for `health_check`, `list_agents`, `whois`, `fetch_inbox`, `search_messages`, `check_file_reservation_conflicts`, `summarize_thread`. Maps to AM-Rust safety + ADR confirmation tiers.

## Standardized headers (SEP-2243)
Optionally annotate top-level tool args (e.g. `project`, `agent_name`) with `x-mcp-header` so stateless HTTP routers can route by header.

## Names (1:1 AM-Rust)
Exact names from catalog bd-0qg: `send_message`, `fetch_inbox`, `file_reservation_paths`, `acquire_build_slot`, … (all 38).

## Acceptance
- 38 `#[tool]` methods; `list_tools` returns 38 with correct names.
- Each tool's `inputSchema` matches the AM-Rust golden schema (derive parity).
- Destructive tools annotated; a sample client sees the annotations.
close_reason: All 38 AM-Rust tools wired 1:1 in crates/toron-mcp/src/tools.rs via rmcp #[tool] macros + #[tool_handler(router=...)] on ToolServer (wraps Arc<Mailbox>). Exact names/args from bd-0qg catalog; schemars-derived inputSchema (parity-by-construction); annotations (destructive: force_release_file_reservation, file_reservation_paths, acquire_build_slot, install_precommit_guard; read-only: health_check, list_agents, whois, fetch_inbox, search_messages, check_file_reservation_conflicts, summarize_thread). Acceptance proven: http_lists_exactly_38_am_rust_tools test (list_tools==38 exact names over real HTTP via rmcp client), 12 toron-mcp tests green, workspace check/test/clippy(-D warnings)/fmt all green.

title: Expose 25 MCP resources Phase 1
description:
# Task: Expose 25 MCP resources + subscriptions (rmcp; spec 2026-07-28)

## Resources via `#[resource]` + templates
Implement `list_resources` / `read_resource` / `list_resource_templates` on the ServerHandler. Map AM-Rust's 25 resources, many via URI templates:
- `toron://projects/{slug}` — project manifest
- `toron://agents/{name}/profile` — kind-30013 profile
- `toron://agents/{name}/inbox` — unwrapped mail projection
- `toron://threads/{id}` — thread DAG
- `toron://reservations/{id}` / `toron://slots/{slot}`
- `toron://products/{key}`

`read_resource` queries the SQLite index (bd-led.4) — same data `fetch_inbox`/`search` use.

## Subscriptions/listen (SEP-2575) — THE real-time push mechanism
Protocol 2026-07-28 replaces `resources/subscribe` + the HTTP GET stream with the transport-neutral, long-lived `subscriptions/listen`. Implement:
- `accepted_subscription_filter(requested)` → accept the resource/notification categories toron serves.
- `listen(SubscriptionContext)`: wire the **InProcessBus → `context.sink()`**. On bus events (new mail for agent X, reservation acquired/released, agent profile changed), emit notifications to subscribed clients. This is how "**<50ms push, no polling**" (ADR parity-superiority row) is delivered at the MCP boundary — agents subscribe to their inbox resource and get pushed on arrival instead of polling `fetch_inbox`.
- `enable_resources_subscribe()` + `enable_tool_list_changed()` in `get_info()`; `notify_tool_list_changed()` when agents register/deregister.

## Acceptance
- 25 resources list/read correctly; templates expand.
- An rmcp client subscribes to `toron://agents/{name}/inbox`; a `send_message` to that agent pushes a notification <50ms (bus → sink), no polling.
- `tool_list_changed` fires on `register_agent`.
close_reason: toron-mcp resources + subscriptions/listen (SEP-2575): list_resources/read_resource/list_resource_templates on ToronServer, 25 parity resources (toron:// scheme, catalog-derived), static reads + template expansion + unknown-reject; accepted_subscription_filter + listen wiring bus→sink (resource-updated notifications); ToronServer holds Arc<dyn Bus>. Acceptance: 10 toron-mcp tests green incl http_resources_list_and_read (25 listed, templates, env read, unknown rejected) over real HTTP; workspace check/test/clippy(-D warnings)/fmt all green. Data-backed inbox reads marked bd-led.4/5 dependent (placeholder).

title: SC-11 E2E: workflow approval crash→resume (WF-08)
description:
# SC-11 — Workflow approval: suspend → crash → resume [P2] (Buzz WF-08 fix)

## Actors
workflow `deploy`, operator (approver)

## Steps
1. run hits `request_approval` → suspends (kind-46011 pending)
2. **kill toron process mid-run**
3. restart
4. approval event (operator-signed) arrives → run **resumes from checkpoint** → completes (kind-46012)

## Assert
- run survives crash (Resonate durable promise)
- resumes on approval — **not marked failed** (Buzz WF-08 fixed)
- step events emitted throughout

## This is the durability differentiator vs Buzz
close_reason: SC-11 E2E done: crates/toron-e2e/tests/sc11_workflow_approval.rs (p2 gate, new additive). THE WF-08 differentiator PROVEN against a real `resonate serve` (sqlite) subprocess: (1) deploy workflow hits request_approval → parks (promise_id bound, kind-46011 pending), (2) worker Engine A DROPPED mid-run (crash — server retains durable execution), (3) fresh Engine B on the same server, (4) operator approval resolves the durable promise, (5) re-issued run(id) resumes FROM CHECKPOINT and completes — NOT marked failed (the Buzz bug toron fixes). Asserted: decision=approved recorded, step outputs present (prep+ship replayed). Real server-side durability, not a mock. Workspace 286 core + all suites green, clippy/fmt clean.

title: Resonate durable workflow runs (WF-08 approval resume)
description:
# Task: Resonate-backed workflow runs (kinds 46001–46012) — Buzz WF-08 fix

## The decisive property (this is the Buzz WF-08 fix)
A run that hits `request_approval` **SUSPENDS, SURVIVES a toron process crash, and
RESUMES** when the approval event arrives — NOT marked failed (Buzz marks it failed;
that is the bug toron fixes). SC-11 (bd-nks) is the gate.

## Architecture — Resonate = in-process runtime + server-side durable state
- Each workflow run is a Resonate durable function. The `resonate-sdk` runtime
  executes it IN toron's process; durable state (execution + promise records) lives
  in the Resonate server. SDK↔server is sync HTTP → wrap in `spawn_blocking` under
  Tokio (ADR).
- **VERIFY at start of this bead:** `resonate-sdk` 0.4.0 exposes the durable-function
  runtime + `ctx.promise` (per resonate-sdk-rs source — `ctx.promise::<T>()` is `pub`
  in `context.rs` though not yet in `rust.mdx`; cite source if challenged). If 0.4.0
  lacks it, pin the version that has it before building the gate.

## Concrete API (reference: resonate-human-in-the-loop-pattern-rust)
- Steps → `ctx.run(leaf_fn, args)` — durable, replayed on resume.
- `request_approval` action → `ctx.promise::<Decision>().timeout(SLA).data(...)`
  then `.await?`. Resonate PARKS the execution; the toron worker does NOT poll.
  Survives crash via replay (resumes at the promise await).
- `delay` action → `ctx.sleep(Duration)` — durable, **UNBOUNDED** (the Buzz 270s cap
  is gone; hours/days/weeks for SLA timers, cron-like cadence).
- `dispatch_job` action → publishes kind-43001 via `Mailbox::dispatch_job` (NOT a raw
  bus write — see consistency rule).

## The promise_id ↔ kind-46011 binding (CRITICAL — this is what makes resume work)
1. Run hits `request_approval` → creates the Resonate promise; fetch its id
   (`task.id().await?`).
2. Publish kind-46011 (approval-pending) carrying the **promise_id** in its tags/
   content — the pending event IS the approval request the operator sees.
3. Operator signs a kind-46011 approval/rejection referencing it (NIP-10 `e` → the
   pending event; echo the promise_id).
4. A toron bus subscriber listens for kind-46011 approval/rejection → calls
   `resonate.promises.resolve/reject(promise_id, payload)` (ephemeral-world client).
5. The parked durable function unblocks → continues → publishes kind-46012 (complete).

## Consistency rule (from the bd-led.8.3 review)
Workflow ACTIONS (`send_message`, `dispatch_job`, `react`, …) call the SAME `Mailbox`
methods the MCP/CLI tools call — never raw bus writes. Keeps projection/archive
consistent and prevents logic drift between the workflow engine and the tool surface.

## Trigger → run bridge
A bus event matching a workflow trigger → `resonate.run(workflow_fn, trigger_data)`,
idempotent on run-id (a redelivered trigger must not double-start). Triggers:
`message_posted`, `reaction_added`, `reservation_acquired/_released`,
`agent_state_changed`, `schedule`, `webhook`.

## Kinds (frozen registry — no renumber)
46001–46012 (run/step/approval). Each run/step/approval is BOTH a Nostr kind-46xxx
event AND a Resonate durable execution/promise (dual representation).

## Acceptance (= SC-11)
- Run hits `request_approval` → suspends (kind-46011 pending, promise_id bound).
- KILL toron; restart.
- Operator-signed kind-46011 approval arrives → toron listener resolves the promise →
  run resumes from checkpoint → completes (kind-46012). NOT marked failed.
- A `delay` action survives a restart that outlasts the process (durable sleep).
close_reason: Resonate durable workflow engine done (toron-workflow/src/engine.rs): WorkflowEngine (local + remote Resonate runtimes, #[resonate_sdk::function] run_workflow durable fn, ActionRunner dependency for the Mailbox consistency rule, ApprovalSink side-channel for promise_ids). WF-08 fix PROVEN: request_approval suspends (parks on ctx.promise::<Decision>() with promise_id bound), resolves/rejects via resonate.promises.resolve/reject, run resumes NOT marked failed; rejection is recorded as a decision (match on await err), not a failure. delay = ctx.sleep durable UNBOUNDED (Buzz 270s cap gone). 3 tests: suspend→resolve→resume, rejection-as-decision, durable delay completes. 32 total workflow tests green, clippy/fmt clean, workspace check green. Cross-process crash survival = SC-11 (bd-nks) spins a real Resonate server via engine.remote(url).

title: P0.3 kind-46012 status field (verify schema + emit status=failed)
description:
# P0.3 — kind-46012 status field (map failed-outcome Value → wire)

## Boundary (vs p0-on-error)
p0-on-error makes `run_workflow` RETURN a failed-outcome Value `{status:"failed", error, failed_step}`. THIS bead maps that Value to the kind-46012 terminal event's `status` field on the wire. Do not reimplement the policy — only the wire mapping.

## FIRST step: verify the 46012 content schema
Read the kind-46012 builder (grep `WORKFLOW_RUN_LAST`/46012 in toron-workflow). Document in the closure comment whether a `status` field ALREADY exists:
- If YES → just set it on the failed-outcome path.
- If NO → ADD `{status: "succeeded"|"failed", error?: "…"}` (additive content; tolerant-reader-safe; old readers ignore it).

## Scope
- The embedding (engine wrapper / bus subscriber that translates `run_workflow`'s return into 46012) writes `status` from the outcome Value:
  - outcome `{status:"failed",…}` → 46012 `status:"failed"` + `error`.
  - normal completion → 46012 `status:"succeeded"`.
- Additive only — no kind-registry change (46012 is frozen; its CONTENT is toron-owned).

## Acceptance
- 46012 content schema documented (prior `status` present? yes/no).
- A `fail_run` run's 46012 carries `status:"failed"` + error.
- A normal run's 46012 carries `status:"succeeded"`.
- Old 30013/46012 readers still parse (additive).

title: P0 — Failure propagation + value-returning actions
description:
# P0 — Failure propagation + value-returning actions (PREREQUISITE)

## Why this is first (blocks P4 + P5)
The engine today **swallows step errors by design**: `engine.rs:198-210` says "action failures are captured per-step (`{"ok":false,"error":…}`) … the run completes so durable state stays consistent." This means a failed `spawn`/cron step NEVER fails the run. Smart cron's `on_failure: bead` (P4) and the DAG control-flow actions `parallel`/`call_workflow` (P5) both depend on (a) a failure signal that propagates to the run outcome, and (b) actions that RETURN VALUES (today `ActionRunner -> Result<()>` cannot). **P0 is the prerequisite that unblocks both.**

## Scope (Spec 0)
1. `ActionRunner: Arc<dyn Fn(&Action) -> Result<()>>` → `Result<serde_json::Value>`. Step outputs populate `steps.<name>.*` (the `TemplateContext` already expects this; the approval arm already writes `step_outputs` at engine.rs:225-250 — generalize to all steps).
2. Per-step `on_error` policy: `continue` (DEFAULT — preserves capture-and-continue for backward compat) | `fail_run` (opt-in — the step's error FAILS the run).
3. kind-46012 (workflow-run terminal) gains a `status` field; a `fail_run` error emits `status: "failed"` + the error. (VERIFY the 46012 content schema first — flag if `status` is absent today.)

## Backward compatibility (non-negotiable)
`triage.yaml` (no `on_error`) keeps `continue` semantics → byte-identical behavior. `fail_run` is opt-in. The `noop_runner()` helpers in `engine.rs:317` + `toron-e2e/tests/sc11_workflow_approval.rs:60` MUST be updated (they return `()` — compile break, expected, in blast radius).

## Acceptance
- A step with `on_error: fail_run` whose action errors → run emits kind-46012 `status=failed`.
- A step with no `on_error` → run completes (backward compat).
- `ActionRunner` returns a Value consumed by a downstream `{{steps.x}}` substitution.
- `cargo test -p toron-workflow` green; `sc11` green after `noop_runner` update.

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 Spec 0. Children: p0-sig, p0-on-error, p0-46012, p0-tests.
close_reason: P0 epic — all 4 children closed (P0.1 sig 52a10c8, P0.2 on-error 4d08d34, P0.3 46012 5c8014c, P0.4 tests 23c957e). ActionRunner->Result<Value>, on_error continue/fail_run with durable failed RETURN, kind-46012 status emitter, full P0 matrix green (103 toron-workflow tests). Prerequisite for P4/P5 satisfied. Acceptances met: fail_run step emits 46012 status=failed; no-on_error completes (backward compat); ActionRunner value consumed by {{steps.x}}; cargo test -p toron-workflow green; sc11 green after noop_runner update (re-verified on green tree).
