title: P0.2 on_error policy (continue default / fail_run) + run-failure propagation
description:
# P0.2 — on_error step policy + run-failure propagation (durable)

## Background
Today the engine ALWAYS captures step errors and completes the run (`engine.rs:198-210`). Smart cron (P4) needs a failed step to FAIL the run so `on_failure: bead` fires. Add an opt-in `on_error` policy.

## CRITICAL: durable-return semantics (not "abort")
`run_workflow` is a `#[resonate_sdk::function]` durable generator — it SUSPENDS (on approval/spawn) and REPLAYS after crash. A "failed run" must be a **deterministic durable return**, NOT a panic/break:
- On `FailRun` + action-Err, `run_workflow` RETURNS a failed-outcome Value: `{"status":"failed","error":"…","failed_step":"upgrade"}`. Returning is durable-safe (replay reproduces the same return, since the action error recurs deterministically at the same step).
- Do NOT `panic!`, `break`, or early-exit the generator mid-step — that corrupts replay. The failure is a VALUE the function returns; the EMBEDDING (engine wrapper / bus subscriber) translates it into the kind-46012 terminal (that wiring is p0-46012, NOT this bead).
- Non-deterministic errors (network flakes): acceptable — on replay the action may succeed, and the run proceeds. That is correct durable behavior (the run reflects the latest attempt). Document this.

## Scope
- Add `on_error: StepOnError` to `Step` (serde default `Continue`):
  - `Continue` (default): error captured as `{"ok":false,"error":…}` in step output; run continues (today's behavior — backward compat).
  - `FailRun`: the run's OUTCOME Value becomes `{status:"failed",…}` and the function returns.
- `run_workflow`: after each action, check `on_error`; on `FailRun`+Err, build + return the failed-outcome Value.
- Lint: `on_error` accepts only `continue`/`fail_run` (typo fail-stop).

## YAML
```yaml
steps:
  - name: upgrade
    action: spawn
    on_error: fail_run      # default omitted => continue
```

## Acceptance
- `on_error: continue` (or omitted) on an erroring step → run completes; step output `{ok:false}` (matches today).
- `on_error: fail_run` on an erroring step → `run_workflow` RETURNS `{status:"failed", error, failed_step}` (the 46012 wiring is p0-46012's acceptance).
- `triage.yaml` (no on_error) unchanged.
- A crash mid-run + resume reproduces the same outcome (deterministic).

## Boundary (do NOT do p0-46012's work here)
This bead produces the failed-outcome VALUE + the on_error policy. It does NOT touch the kind-46012 wire schema — that is p0-46012 (which maps this Value to the terminal `status` field). Keep the boundary crisp to avoid double-implementation.

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 Spec 0. Depends on p0-sig (value-returning runner).
close_reason: on_error continue(default)/fail_run + durable run-failure RETURN. fail_run+err -> {status:failed,error,failed_step} deterministic return (not panic). Default continue = backward compat. Strict enum = typo fail-stop. TDD RED->GREEN; 82 tests. Commit 4d08d34. (46012 wire is bd-p0-46012-on1.)

title: P0.1 ActionRunner Result<()>→Result<Value> + noop_runner updates
description:
# P0.1 — ActionRunner signature: Result<()> → Result<Value>

## Background
`toron-workflow/src/engine.rs:80`: `pub type ActionRunner = Arc<dyn Fn(&Action) -> anyhow::Result<()> + Send + Sync>;`. Steps cannot return outputs. The approval arm already manually writes `step_outputs` (engine.rs:225-250); generalize so EVERY action returns a Value that flows into `steps.<name>` for downstream templates/guards.

## Scope
- Change the type alias to `Result<serde_json::Value>`.
- Update `run_workflow` to insert each step's returned Value into `step_outputs` under the step's `name` (or index).
- Update the two `noop_runner()` helpers: `engine.rs:317` (in-module test) + `toron-e2e/tests/sc11_workflow_approval.rs:60` — return `Ok(serde_json::Value::Null)`.
- Existing actions: `Delay`→Null, `RequestApproval`→the decision object (already), `Send*`/`React`/`DispatchJob`/`CallWebhook`→a small status object `{ok:true}` or Null.

## Acceptance
- Workspace compiles (`cargo check --workspace`).
- A synthetic action returning `{"n":42}` is readable as `{{steps.foo.n}}` in a later step's template.
- `sc11_workflow_approval` passes after the helper update.

## Considerations
- This is an engine-signature break (in blast radius) — workspace-internal only, NOT a wire change.
- Do NOT change the on-wire kind-46012 shape here (that's p0-46012).

## This task (cancel-safety / reentrancy - guard held across .await)
`.await` while holding a std::sync::Mutex (impossible - std guard isn't Send
across await in tokio) or tokio::sync::Mutex guard.

## Method
1. ast-grep `.lock().await` - each is a tokio guard held across await.
2. For each: is the held-across-await intentional (serialized section) or
   accidental (long-held lock blocking other tasks)? Cancel-safety: if the
   task is cancelled mid-await, is the guard dropped cleanly (RAII) or leaked?
3. tokio::sync::Mutex is cancel-safe (guard Drop on cancel). std is not held
   across await (compiler rejects). So focus on tokio guard contention.

## Success criteria
Findings table: each `.lock().await` site classified intentional-vs-accidental
+ contention note.

## Considerations
Related to p1-std-guard-across-blockon (the ast-grep-invisible sibling) -
together they cover the full held-guard-during-blocking surface.

title: P1 — Backend trait unification (one trait, by design)
description:
# P1 — Backend trait unification (ONE trait, by design — not "mechanical")

## Why
flywheel ships a DUPLICATE `MultiplexerBackend` (`flywheel/src/backend/mod.rs:204`: object-safe, `&mut self`, 18 methods, every method `Unsupported`-defaults, ~20 call sites) AND toron-core has `Backend` (`crates/toron-core/src/backend/mod.rs`: native AFIT, `&self`, 6 methods, no defaults, "never used as a dyn"). These are **structurally incompatible** — NOT a mechanical merge. The herdr *client* is already unified (`flywheel/herdr_shim.rs:31` re-exports `toron_core::backend::herdr`); only the TRAIT SURFACE is duplicated. This is the concrete source of the captain's "churn."

## Scope (ADR-0005 P1)
1. **Decide** the unified trait design: object-safety (keep `dyn`-capable?), `&self` vs `&mut self`, whether to keep `Unsupported`-default openness (ADR-0002 §6 "open-to-extension, not sealed"), and `MailBackend` fate (unify alongside, or explicitly scope out).
2. Land ONE `Backend` trait in `toron-core::backend`; delete flywheel's duplicate.
3. Migrate the ~20 `&mut dyn MultiplexerBackend` call sites in flywheel (`main.rs` durable-loop leaf handlers).
4. Verify by call-site migration compiling, NOT by a grep for a deleted name.

## Acceptance
- `flywheel backend list` shows ONE trait source.
- All ~20 former `&mut dyn` call sites compile against the unified trait.
- `MailBackend` fate documented (unified or explicitly out-of-scope).
- `flywheel deps` protocol line unchanged; herdr client still single-source.

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 P1 (amends ADR-0002 Backend trait ownership). Children: p1-design, p1-unify, p1-verify.
close_reason: P1 complete. All 3 children closed: bd-p1-design-gn0 (unified trait design record, 287a698), bd-p1-unify-y9j (sync &self object-safe Backend in toron-core + flywheel migration, ~20 call sites, duplicate MultiplexerBackend deleted), bd-p1-verify-16v (verified: workspace green, no local trait def, backend list healthy, 251 flywheel tests). ONE Backend trait by design; MailBackend explicitly deferred (P1.1 decision #7).

misses events with no signal.

   add a metric for ops.

log/metric) + fix in batch.

Flywheel boundary (relay_bus is toron-core, consumed by flywheel daemon mode)

title: P1.1 Unified Backend trait design (obj-safety/&self/method-set/Unsupported/MailBackend)
description:
# P1.1 — Unified Backend trait design decision

## Scope
Produce a short design record (comment in `toron-core/src/backend/mod.rs` + a closure note on this bead) deciding:
- **Object-safety:** keep the trait `dyn`-capable (flywheel needs `Box<dyn MultiplexerBackend>` at ~20 sites)? Recommend: YES — the cost is no-generic-async-fns, acceptable.
- **Receiver:** `&self` (toron-core) or `&mut self` (flywheel's stateful socket clients w/ per-call request ids)? Recommend: `&self` + interior mutability (`Mutex`/`tokio::sync` inside the impl) — matches toron-core's stance, keeps `&self` shareable.
- **Method set:** the superset (flywheel's 18: workspace/pane/agent/subscribe) — toron-core's 6 (spawn/prompt/wait/read/send_keys/events) are a subset.
- **Defaults:** keep `Unsupported`-default openness (ADR-0002 §6) so future backends inherit `Unsupported`.
- **`MailBackend`:** unify alongside (same pattern) OR explicitly defer (document which).

## Acceptance
- Design record committed; the 4 decisions (obj-safety, receiver, method-set, defaults) + MailBackend fate written down.
- Reviewed by the captain before p1-unify starts.

## Considerations
- Do NOT start migrating (p1-unify) until this design is agreed — the migration shape depends on it.
close_reason: Design record committed (287a698). 7 decisions: 1) object-safety YES (dyn-capable, Box<dyn Backend> at ~20 sites); 2) receiver &self + interior mutability (Mutex-wrapped clients, matches toron-core HerdrBackend); 3) SYNC execution (all ~20 real call sites are sync CLI commands / hidden subprocess leaves; async toron-core Backend has ZERO production trait callers — verified — so no runtime-forcing churn); 4) method set = flywheel 18-superset (name+workspace/pane/agent/prompt_coded/subscribe), toron-core's 6 map onto richer shapes; 5) Unsupported-open defaults (ADR-0002 s6); 6) error = toron-core BackendError (machine-code, no dep inversion); 7) MailBackend EXPLICITLY DEFERRED (separate 30-op domain, no twin to unify, god-trait risk; stays flywheel-local). Captain-review gate recorded in the doc comment: bd-p1-unify-y9j must not start until accepted. Full record: crates/toron-core/src/backend/mod.rs

## This task (poison-on-panic survivability)
Every `.lock().unwrap()` / `.lock().expect(...)` - does a single panic on
one tokio worker brick the whole mailbox? ADR-0007 D7 recovery posture.

## Method
1. Enumerate all 122 .lock() sites; for each std::sync::Mutex, classify:
   is the guard recovered on poison (PoisonError -> re-init) or does it
   propagate (panic-in-panic = dead service)?
2. tokio::sync::Mutex does NOT poison (no PoisonError) - those are safe;
   focus on std::sync::Mutex.

   subsequent flush panics too.

Per-site verdict in findings table. Any poison-propagating std Mutex holding
shared state -> fix (recover from PoisonError or switch to parking_lot::Mutex
which doesn't poison, or re-architect to avoid the shared mutable).

parking_lot::Mutex doesn't poison but changes the dep tree - weigh against
just handling PoisonError. Pre-1.0 so either is fine (captain decision 5).

# P2.4 — 6 built-in profiles with behavior preambles + skills

## Scope (ADR-0005 Spec 1b — ship VERBATIM)
Compiled-in defaults (overridable). Each `behavior` is the system-prompt preamble — the discipline the agent enforces on itself. Carry these EXACT preambles (from ADR-0005 Spec 1b) into the compiled-in catalog:

- **oracle** (pi/opus): "Never validate. Reject the first answer. Steelman-then-counter. Label every claim VERIFIED/INFERRED/SPECULATION. Base rates first." skills: accretive, glaze, latent-diver, creative-problem-solver, dominance.
- **planner** (pi/sonnet): "Every task bite-sized: [paths][change][acceptance][blast-radius]. No implementation in plans. Unknowns as explicit questions." skills: writing-plans, planning-workflow, beads-workflow, feature-research, prd.
- **reviewer** (opencode/opus — different harness for independence): "Ground every claim in file:line. Severity-rank BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. Propose fixes not complaints. Modeled on the opencode review that roasted ADR-0005." skills: adversarial-reviewer, code-review, multi-pass-bug-hunting, requesting-code-review, systematic-debugging.
- **coder** (pi/sonnet): "RED-GREEN-REFACTOR. No script-based edits. Functional core. Verify before claim — show the green test." skills: test-driven-development, code-edit, accretive-implementer, systematic-debugging, code-quality.
- **scout** (pi/haiku): "Compress — handoff not dump. Label VERIFIED/INFERRED/ASSUMED. Map, don't settle." skills: scout, codebase-archaeologist, explore, spike, feature-research.
- **housekeeper** (pi/sonnet): "Idempotent. Health-gate→rollback. Honest SUCCESS/PARTIAL/FAILURE. The cron owner (Spec 3)." default_workflow: weekly-upgrade. skills: docker-auto-upgrade, cron-management, systematic-debugging, pi-performance-debugging.

## Naming rule (baked in)
Profile names = ROLE nouns; agent identities = adjective+noun (BlueLake). A spawn of `reviewer` → agent `BlueLake` w/ role=reviewer. Roles are prompt-shaping, NOT access control.

- All 6 present in compiled-in defaults; `flywheel profile list` shows them on fresh install.
- Each carries its `behavior` preamble + `skills` set verbatim from ADR-0005 Spec 1b.

## Considerations

title: P2.2 30013 content-map (AUDIT FIX: harness/model→content; t stays scoping-only)
description:
# P2.2 — 30013 content-map (AUDIT FIX) — full content path + no-overload guard

## Background (Review Log round 6 — the protocol audit catch)
Spec 1 v1 proposed "harness/model/role as `t`-tags" on kind-30013. WRONG twice:
1. **Collision:** `bus/scoping.rs:26` emits `["t", <project-slug>]` on every non-hidden event for project scoping. Overloading `t` → project filters return false matches.
2. **Redundant:** `AgentProfile` (`nostr/identity.rs:31`) ALREADY carries `program` (= harness) + `model` in the 30013 **content JSON**.

## Scope (the FULL content path — this is the protocol-safety bead, own it end-to-end)
1. **Mapping:** flywheel `Profile.harness` → `AgentProfile.program`; `Profile.model` → `AgentProfile.model`. (Both fields EXIST — a mapping, not a schema change.)
2. **MCP tool args:** `register_agent` / `create_agent_identity` (`toron-mcp/src/tools.rs:542/564`) must EXPOSE `program`/`model` as OPTIONAL args (additive — old callers omit them; the 38-tool COUNT is unchanged, ADR-0005 invariant 3 holds). A captain sets harness/model via the tool → the builder writes them into 30013 content.
3. **Builder:** confirm `build_profile_event` serializes `program`/`model` into content (it already serializes `AgentProfile` — just ensure the fields populate).
4. **Catalog-only fields:** `role`/`behavior`/`backend`/`default_workflow` are flywheel-catalog-only — NEVER on the bus.
5. **`t` tag stays project-scoping-only.** No new tags on 30013.
6. **Test `profile_no_tag_overload`:** a profile publish → 30013 whose ONLY `t` tag is the project slug; harness/model present in CONTENT.

## Acceptance
- `register_agent {name, program:"pi", model:"claude-sonnet-4"}` → 30013 content has `program`/`model`; `t` tags = [project slug] only.
- `profile_no_tag_overload` green (forever — the protocol guard).
- Old 30013 readers (ignoring program/model) still parse.
- The 38-tool count unchanged; the 2 tools gained optional args only.

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 Spec 1 (Revision 5 correction). Flag for captain review before close (protocol-safety).
close_reason: Protocol-safety audit fix landed (toron e2874be). 1) MCP register_agent/create_agent_identity: program/model args now OPTIONAL (additive — old callers omit them; 38-tool count unchanged). 2) profile_no_tag_overload guard test GREEN: harness/model present in 30013 CONTENT (build_profile_event serializes AgentProfile.program/model), the ONLY t tag is the project slug — no tag overload, no false-match on project filters. 3) Verified t stays scoping-only (bus/scoping.rs). Catalog-only fields (role/behavior/backend/default_workflow) never on bus. FLAG FOR CAPTAIN REVIEW per bead (protocol-safety).

title: P2 — Agent Profiles + built-in library (6 roles)
description:
# P2 — Agent Profiles + built-in library

## Why
Profiles are the captain's "agent crew" vocabulary — a named, reusable agent composition layering spawn-intent on the existing kind-30013 identity. A **Profile** = role template; an **agent** = instance (auto adjective+noun identity). Spawning the `reviewer` profile yields an agent like `BlueLake` running `role=reviewer`. Roles are prompt-shaping labels, NEVER access control (contact-policy + file-reservations remain the enforcement layer).

## Scope (ADR-0005 Spec 1 + Spec 1b)
- flywheel profile catalog (`~/.config/flywheel/profiles.toml`, overridable; compiled-in defaults).
- **30013 content-map** (THE AUDIT FIX, Review Log round 6): flywheel `harness`/`model` map to the EXISTING `AgentProfile.program`/`.model` content fields. `t` tag stays project-scoping-only. role/behavior/backend/default_workflow are flywheel-catalog-only (never on the bus).
- `Profile::resolve("@name")` → `(npub, SpawnSpec)` with project→host scope + signing context.
- 6 built-in profiles (oracle/planner/reviewer/coder/scout/housekeeper) with tuned `behavior` preambles + `skills` sets.
- `flywheel profile` CLI.

## Audit fix (critical — DO NOT regress)
Spec 1 originally said "harness/model/role as t-tags." WRONG: `bus/scoping.rs:26` already uses `["t", <slug>]` for project scoping (overloading breaks project filters) AND `AgentProfile.program`/`.model` already carry harness/model in 30013 content (`nostr/identity.rs:31`). Fix: content-map; t stays scoping-only; test `profile_no_tag_overload`.

## Acceptance (per child bead)
- `flywheel profile list` shows the 6 built-ins on a fresh install.
- `Profile::resolve` returns correct (npub, SpawnSpec) with project-vs-host signing context.
- `profile_no_tag_overload` green (30013 never carries harness/model/role as t-tags).

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 Spec 1 + Spec 1b. Children: p2-catalog, p2-content-map, p2-resolve, p2-builtins, p2-tests, p2-cli.
close_reason: P2 complete. All 6 children closed: catalog-9by (profiles.toml + compiled-in defaults), content-map-msp (30013 content-map audit fix, t stays scoping-only), resolve-ntt (Profile::resolve project->host + SpawnSpec + SigningContext), builtins-3zl (6 built-in profiles, verbatim Spec 1b preambles + skills), cli-wn8 (flywheel profile CLI list/show/create/edit/run), tests-4bd (profile_resolve_scope + profile_no_tag_overload green). Verified: 251 flywheel tests green, workspace clean, profile_no_tag_overload guards the protocol forever.

title: P2.3 Profile::resolve (project→host scope, @name, SpawnSpec, signing context)
description:
# P2.3 — Profile::resolve (project→host scope, @name, SpawnSpec, signing context)

## Scope
- `Profile::resolve(project, "@name") -> (npub, SpawnSpec, SigningContext)`.
- **Scope order: project → host.** Project-scoped profile resolves via that project's kind-30013 (`d=project-slug:name`); host-scoped (catalog default) resolves via the operator identity.
- `SigningContext`: operator key (host scope) vs project agent key (project scope) — determines who signs the run's events.
- `SpawnSpec{harness, model, backend}` feeds `Backend::spawn`.
- Unknown `@name` → fail-fast (AM-Rust parity).

## Acceptance
- `@housekeeper` in a `scope: project` cron resolves to the project's 30013 + project agent signing context.
- `@housekeeper` in a `scope: host` cron resolves via operator identity.
- Unknown name → error (no silent fallback).

## Considerations
- Depends on p2-catalog + p2-content-map (the content fields it reads).
close_reason: Profile::resolve landed (flywheel 8140dd0). ProfileCatalog::resolve(@name, project_scope, operator_npub, project_resolver) implements ADR-0005 Spec 1 resolution: project scope -> project kind-30013 (injected DI seam reading toron_core::nostr::identity::resolve_name) with ProjectAgent signing context; host scope (None) -> operator identity with Operator signing context. Returns ResolvedProfile{npub, SpawnSpec{harness,model,backend}, signing}. Unknown name / unregistered in project -> fail-fast (AM-Rust parity). Acceptance met: @housekeeper project-scope resolves to project 30013 + project agent signing; host-scope resolves via operator; unknown errors. 4 TDD tests green; full flywheel suite 247 green; clippy clean.

title: P3.6 auto-crew / smart steering (crew:auto infer + explicit + @crew.r + park/reap)
description:
# P3.6 — auto-crew / smart steering (Spec 4c) — staged delivery

## Why (captain's directive #3)
The orchestrator smartly steers the crew FROM the workflow. The captain writes INTENT (roles + fan-out); flywheel handles spawn-count, distribution, collection, parking, reap.

## Scope (P3 delivers this)
- `crew:` field on Workflow:
  - **Explicit:** `crew: { planner: 1, coder: 2, reviewer: 1, scout: 1 }` → flywheel spawns the squad once, binds `@crew.<role>`.
  - **Auto:** `crew: auto` → infer members from the workflow's `profile:` refs (count = max parallelism the graph demands). Zero-config (debate/brainstorm).
- `parallel over: "@crew.coder"` → fans a step across all coders; collected into a list under `steps.<name>`.
- Idle crew parked (not killed); reaped at run end (or `retain_crew: true`).

## STAGED DELIVERY (honest — do not overclaim at P3)
- **At P3:** `parallel over:` dispatches to crew members and COLLECTS results, but **sequentially or via tokio tasks** (NOT durable-concurrent-within-one-run). Correct, observable, just not concurrent-fan-out.
- **At P5 (gated on p5-spike):** TRUE durable-concurrent fan-out within one Resonate run (the spike proves replay-determinism). Until P5 lands, `debate`/`brainstorm` run their panel sequentially — functionally complete, latency-suboptimal.
- This staging is why p3-zero-config's `debate` test accepts degraded-until-P5.

## Acceptance
- `crew: auto` infers members from steps (`crew_auto_infer`).
- Explicit `crew:` spawns the squad; `@crew.r` binds (`crew_explicit`).
- Idle crew parked + reaped (`crew_lifecycle`).

# P3 — Unified workflow engine (one vocabulary, one engine)

## Why (Revision 5 unification)
Revision 5 converged flywheel's imperative `Workflows`/`Pipelines`/`Recipe` and toron's durable engine into **ONE concept: workflow, on ONE engine (toron-workflow, Resonate)**. The captain's mental model: workflow = named, purpose-driven, multi-step procedure. flywheel routes ALL workflow execution through `WorkflowEngine` via a real cargo edge (the `flywheel → toron-workflow` arrow that ADR-0003's diagram implied but no Cargo.toml wired). flywheel's `WorkflowStep::Send/Wait` → step types; `pipeline` → a `call_workflow` chain; `Recipe` → squad (P6).

## Scope (ADR-0005 Spec 2, 2a, 2b, 4c)
- cargo edge (flywheel deps toron-workflow) + `WorkflowEngine::invoke`.
- workflow catalog (`workflows/*.yaml`) + absorb legacy `workflows.toml`/`pipelines.toml`.
- stage library (`stages.toml` + compiled-in `STAGES` p1-p6/p8 + semantic aliases).
- `trigger: Option<Trigger>` (invoke-only workflows).
- 5 built-in workflows (brainstorm/plan/beads/debate/goal) + triage.
- auto-crew (Spec 4c): orchestrator smart-steers the crew from the workflow; parallel/fan-out.
- toron workflow CLI + flywheel workflow CLI.
- zero-config default config (compiled-in profiles/stages/workflows; fresh-install contract).

## Why unify (vs sibling vocabularies — the captain's directive)
Seamless integration: `flywheel workflow run <name>` regardless of simple-sends vs complex-fan-out; durable by default; crash-survivable always. Resonate in-process is cheap enough that a 3-step Send/Wait workflow pays negligible overhead and gains crash survival.

## Acceptance (per child)
- `flywheel workflow run debate` works on a FRESH install (zero-config) — spawns the crew + runs.
- flywheel's legacy `workflows.toml`/`pipelines.toml` parse + run through the one engine (captain's live runs survive).
- `toron workflow invoke triage.yaml --inputs '{}'` starts a run.
- `flywheel/Cargo.toml` lists `toron-workflow`.

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 Spec 2/2a/2b/4c + Revision 5. Depends on P1 (backend) + P2 (profiles). Children: p3-edge, p3-catalog, p3-stages, p3-trigger-opt, p3-builtins, p3-auto-crew, p3-cli, p3-zero-config, p3-tests.

title: P4.4 bead-on-failure + defined-fixer + repeat-failure escalate
description:
# P4.4 — bead-on-failure + defined-fixer + repeat-failure escalate

## Scope (the loop closure — Spec 3)
On a FAILED cron run (kind-46012 status=failed, from P0):
1. **bead:** flywheel runs `br create` with the failure bundle (run-id, workflow, owner, error, last-known-good, retry history) → a triageable bead.
2. **defined-fixer:** flywheel invokes the owner profile's diagnosis workflow (a workflow the captain authors, e.g. `housekeeper-diagnose.yaml`) → the profile proposes a patch (PR / fix-bead / config edit). If NO diagnosis workflow is registered for the owner, the loop is explicitly HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP (the bead waits for `flywheel work ready`).
3. **repeat-failure:** `repeat_failure ≥ repeat_threshold` → escalate (kind-14 DM to captain, importance=high, ack_required).

## Acceptance
- `cron_failure_bead` (FW): failed run → `br` bead created with full bundle.
- `cron_escalate` (FW): repeat_threshold consecutive failures → kind-14 DM to captain.
- No diagnosis workflow → bead waits (documented human-in-loop, NOT silent).

## Considerations
- Depends on p4-cron-mgr + p0-46012 (the failure status) + p0-on-error.
- The fixer workflow is the missing dependency of the "killer feature" — p4-migrate-sagas authors one for housekeeper.
close_reason: P4.4 decision layer complete (toron side). cron_failure.rs: pure evaluate() (on_failure -> on_repeat_failure at exact repeat_threshold; on_success resets streak; threshold 0 clamps to 1), is_failed()/failure_details() on the kind-46012 failed shape, FailureBundle, PolicyEvent, distinct-newtype PolicySink (TypeId-safe). cron_loop records a PolicyEvent (action + full bundle: run-id, workflow, owner, error, failed_step, consecutive) per tick onto the sink; the embedding (flywheel) executes the side effects (br create bead / kind-14 escalate DM) per ADR-0003 3A. Consecutive streak is a durable loop local (fresh loop starts at 1, no double-count across replay). PolicySink registered on the engine. Rows green at the decision level: cron_failure_bead (sc22) + cron_escalate (sc23, N-1 log / N-th escalate at threshold) un-ignored; 6 unit tests; 123 toron-workflow tests; full e2e suite green. HONEST SCOPE: the acceptance wording 'flywheel runs br create' / 'kind-14 DM' — the flywheel side-effect EXECUTION (reading the sink, calling br/DM) is the embedding's wiring, not landed here; the DECISION contract + acceptance behavior are proven. Commit 6777408.

title: P4.3 cron manager (Resonate durable-sleep + latest catch-up + restart survival)
description:
# P4.3 — cron manager (Resonate durable-sleep + latest catch-up + restart survival)

## Scope (scheduler durability — Spec 3)
- The cron manager is a **Resonate durable-sleep loop** (`ctx.sleep` until next tick — the unbounded-sleep capability ADR-0003 ships), NOT a wall-clock assumption.
- Missed-tick policy = `latest` (run the most-recent due tick on wake), configurable.
- On flywheel restart, the loop resumes from durable state (no double-fire; idempotent on run_id).

## Acceptance
- `cron_catchup` (FW): flywheel down at due time → on wake, runs the latest due tick (not all missed).
- `cron_restart` (FW): restart mid-window → loop resumes, no duplicate runs.
- `cron_success` (FW): owner spawns → runs → SUCCESS → `on_success: log`.

## Considerations
- Depends on p4-schedule-ext + p4-spawn-await (the run uses spawn).
- This is the "scheduler is durable" guarantee — without it, cron is fire-and-forget again.
close_reason: P4.3 complete. Cron manager landed (toron-workflow/src/cron.rs): Resonate durable-sleep loop (cron_loop ctx.sleep until next tick -> fire owning workflow as durable child via ctx.run -> advance checkpoint). Restart survival + no-double-fire via Resonate replay (re-invoking cron:{name} resumes the same loop; deterministic child ids). Missed-tick policy = latest (latest_due_at_or_before: most-recent due tick at-or-before now, one run on wake, no burst). next_due/normalize_cron parse 5-field vixie in toron (no flywheel import per ADR-0003 3A); CronRegistry DI seam bridges flywheel's crons.toml. Acceptance rows green: cron_success + cron_restart (sc21_cron_durable_loop), cron_catchup (sc24, un-ignored), 7 cron unit tests, 117 toron-workflow tests, full e2e suite green. Commit: fea9c4f (P4.3). sc22/sc23 remain P4.4-owned skeletons.

# P4.5 — migrate docker-auto-upgrade + agent-reach-upgrade sagas → workflows

## Scope (the generalization target)
Convert the captain's two hand-built self-reporting cron sagas into declarative workflows owned by `housekeeper`:
- `docker-upgrade.yaml` — the weekly docker image upgrade (snapshot → pull/rebuild → recreate → health-gate 90s → auto-rollback-on-fail). Owned by housekeeper; `on_failure: bead`.
- `agent-reach-upgrade.yaml` — weekly agent-reach CLI upgrade + verify.
- `housekeeper-diagnose.yaml` — the defined-fixer (p4-bead-on-fail): on a failure bead, housekeeper reads the bundle + proposes a patch.

## Sequencing rule (no mid-migration gap)
The new workflow path must pass the SAME health-gates as the saga BEFORE the old systemd-timer path is removed.

## Acceptance
- `docker-upgrade` workflow passes the same health-gates as the bash saga (aiostreams/resonate/honcho/dnscrypt/pihole).
- `housekeeper-diagnose` produces a diagnosable patch-bead on a simulated failure.
- Old systemd timers remain until the workflow is verified (then disable, don't delete).

## Considerations
- Depends on p4-cron-mgr + p4-bead-on-fail. This is the proof the framework replaces the hand-built sagas.
close_reason:
P4.5 migration delivered + verified (flywheel af61df1, toron 57523a3). Workflow definitions owned by housekeeper wired through the landed P4.3 cron manager + P4.4 policy.

DELIVERED:
1. flywheel/src/cron.rs: registrations()/registrations_from() (merged view -> CronRegistration with catalog-resolved Workflows); cron_runner() (real HTTP health probes, 5s timeout, unreachable probe = Err so on_error: fail_run fails the run); spawn_failure_bead()/failure_bead_fields() (br create with the full FailureBundle embedded — run_id/workflow/owner/error/failed_step/consecutive, returns bead id); start_loops() (engine local + CronRegistry + CronManager::new().start() durable-sleep loops + PolicySink drain -> bead side-effects).
2. main.rs: CronCmd::Start dispatch.
3. toron/workflows/docker-upgrade.yaml: explicit health-gate probes for the saga's five services (aiostreams:3000, resonate:8001, honcho:8010 POST, pihole:80, dnscrypt:5053), each on_error: fail_run — the SAME health-gates as the bash saga (P4.5 sequencing rule). agent-reach-upgrade + housekeeper-diagnose unchanged (already carry policy + defined-fixer flow).

VERIFIED:
- Tests: 19 cron unit (runner live-probe, health-gate all-up passes / one-down fails, failure-bead bundle content, registrations) + 4 smart_cron (incl. deployed-YAML structure gate: 5 probes, on_error fail_run, owner housekeeper, on_failure bead) + full flywheel suite green (286 bin, 6/8/2/3). toron workspace check green.
- LIVE: flywheel cron start fired the durable loop at the minute boundary; docker-upgrade ran; gates failed (services down on this host); failure bead created with the full diagnosable bundle (bd-w0cz — verified then deleted).

# P4.1 — schedule trigger extension (owner + policy + no_claim_timeout + scope)

## Scope (ADR-0005 Spec 3)

```yaml
trigger:
```

description:
# P4 — Smart cron (self-reporting + defined fixer; honest scope)

## Why (the captain's directive #3 generalizes the hand-built sagas)
The captain runs two bespoke self-reporting crons today: `docker-auto-upgrade` (systemd timer + 200-line bash saga w/ health-gates + auto-rollback) + `agent-reach-upgrade` (systemd user timer). Both are the SAME shape: schedule → run → health-gate → on-failure-act. Smart cron makes that shape declarative + uniform: one workflow per maintenance job, one owning profile, one failure→bead policy.

## Honest scope (Review Log round 2 — RETRACT "self-healing")
v1 called this "self-healing." It is **self-reporting + defined-triage**. The loop closes only because a *defined fixer* (the owning profile's diagnosis workflow) consumes the failure bead. Without that fixer, the failure moves one hop (cron→bead→nobody). p4-bead-on-fail defines the fixer (or the loop is explicitly human-in-loop).

## Scope (ADR-0005 Spec 3)
- schedule trigger extension: `owner` (profile), `policy{on_failure, on_repeat_failure, repeat_threshold, on_success, max_retries, no_claim_timeout}`, `scope: host|project`.
- `spawn` action + promise↔job binding (bus subscriber on 43004/43006) + no_claim_timeout abort.
- cron manager = Resonate durable-sleep loop + `latest` catch-up + restart survival.
- bead-on-failure (`br create`) + defined-fixer workflow + repeat-failure escalate (kind-14 DM).
- migrate docker-auto-upgrade + agent-reach-upgrade → workflow templates.
- `flywheel cron` CLI.

## Acceptance (per child)
- A cron with `on_failure: bead` whose run fails (P0 status=failed) produces a `br` bead.
- `no_claim_timeout: 600` spawn-await aborts after 10m unclaimed.
- docker-auto-upgrade template passes the same health-gates as the saga.
- Scheduler survives a flywheel restart (durable-sleep + latest catch-up).

## Governed-by

title: P4.2 spawn action + promise↔job binding (bus subscriber 43004/43006) + no_claim_timeout
description:
# P4.2 — spawn action + promise↔job binding + no_claim_timeout

## Background (distinct from approval — Spec 4a)
`spawn await` is NOT the approval-promise mechanism verbatim:
- approval: resolver is an OPERATOR who will act; rejection = DECISION (run continues); no timeout.
- spawn-await: resolver is an AGENT that must CLAIM+complete a job; failure = FAILURE (run fails, Spec 0); `no_claim_timeout` aborts.

## Scope
- `spawn` action: resolve `profile` via injected ProfileResolver (DI seam, never a flywheel import in toron) → Backend::spawn → emit kind-43001 carrying `promise_id` in its `spec`.
- **promise↔job binding subsystem:** a bus subscriber watches kind-43004 (result) / 43006 (error); on arrival resolves the parked promise via `resonate.promises.resolve/reject`.
- `await: true` → run SUSPENDS on the promise; `no_claim_timeout` → reject with `timeout` → step fails → Spec 0 propagates.

## Acceptance
- `spawn_await_resume` (SC): run suspends, resumes on 43004.
- `spawn_await_failure` (SC): 43006 → run FAILS (not a decision).
- `spawn_no_claim_timeout` (UT): unclaimed past timeout → abort → fail.

## Considerations
- Depends on P0 (failure propagation). ProfileResolver is `Arc<dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<(npub, SpawnSpec)>>` — same DI idiom as ActionRunner.
close_reason: P4.2 complete. All three acceptances green: spawn_await_resume (SC-19 e2e + unit), spawn_await_failure (SC-20 e2e + unit), spawn_no_claim_timeout (SC-18). Root-caused + fixed the 0.6-migration approval/spawn park regression: ApprovalSink and SpawnSink were the same concrete type, colliding in the Resonate TypeId-keyed dependency map (spawn sink shadowed approval sink) — now distinct newtypes with Deref. 110 toron-workflow unit tests + sc11/sc18/sc19/sc20 e2e green. Commits a1fe947 (engine), bac295b (WIP), 90359c3 (sink fix).

description:
# P5 — Engine flexibility (GATED on the Resonate concurrency spike)

## Why (captain's directive: engine is "static")
Today a Workflow is one trigger + one guard + a flat `Vec<Step>` of 7 fixed actions. No fan-out, branching, retries, sub-workflow calls. The captain wants it much more flexible — backward-compatibly.

## The GATE (do NOT skip)
Resonate's Rust SDK is early-development (0.4.x). Concurrent durable children that each suspend on an external promise, INSIDE one deterministic-replay function, is NOT a documented primitive. **p5-spike MUST pass before any P5 schema lands.** If the spike fails, P5 is deferred (not blocking P0-P4 + P6 value).

## Scope (ADR-0005 Spec 4b)
- `graph:` DAG (nodes + `needs:`; edges DERIVED from needs — dual encoding dropped).
- control-flow actions: `parallel`, `branch`, `retry`, `foreach`, `call_workflow`, `spawn`.
- `parallel over: "@crew.r"` (fan-out) + `over: <N>` (elastic) — integrates auto-crew (p3-auto-crew).
- lint-graph (acyclic, needs resolvable, no orphans).

## Backward compat
`steps:` (linear) stays — `triage.yaml` parses + runs identically. `graph:` is opt-in.

## Governed-by
ADR-0005 Spec 4b. Depends on P0 (value-returning actions) + P3 (engine). Children: p5-spike (GATE), p5-graph, p5-actions, p5-lint, p5-tests.
close_reason: P5 epic — all 5 children closed (P5.1 spike GATE 9192b1d PASS 5/5 deterministic, P5.2 graph 4a41719, P5.3 actions 9fd70cc, P5.4 lint in graph bead, P5.5 tests 2a1225c). GATE satisfied: Resonate concurrency + replay-determinism spike PASSED before the graph schema landed. graph: DAG (nodes+needs, edges derived), control-flow actions (retry/branch/foreach/parallel/call_workflow), lint-graph (acyclic/needs/orphan). Acceptances met: independent nodes run concurrently; cyclic graph rejected by lint; edges derived from needs (no edges: field); 103 toron-workflow tests + sc16/sc17 e2e green. Deferred: call_workflow sub-run wiring + @crew.r durable fan-out (orchestrator seam).

```yaml
graph:
  nodes:
    scout: { action: spawn, profile: "@scout", workflow: reproduce, await: true }
    plan:  { action: spawn, profile: "@planner", await: true, needs: [scout] }
```

title: P5.1 Resonate concurrency + replay-determinism spike (GATE — must pass before P5 schema)
description:
# P5.1 — Resonate concurrency + replay-determinism spike (GATE)

## Why this gates P5
Concurrent durable children that each suspend on an external promise, inside ONE deterministic-replay function, must replay BIT-IDENTICALLY after a crash. Resonate's Rust SDK (0.4.x) does not document this primitive. If it can't be proven, the DAG engine is unsafe (non-deterministic replay = corrupted durable state).

## Run this EARLY (de-risking) — in parallel with P0-P2
This bead has NO upstream deps. **Kick it off alongside P0** so its pass/fail result is known BEFORE the captain sinks the P3-P4 investment that P5 extends. If it FAILS: P5 (DAG/concurrent fan-out) is deferred; `parallel over:` stays sequential (p3-auto-crew staging); the captain re-plans. If it PASSES: P5 proceeds as the final phase. Either way, early knowledge is cheap; late knowledge is expensive.

## Scope (the spike test)
An SC-style test in toron-e2e:
- A graph run with TWO concurrent nodes, BOTH suspending on external promises.
- Resolve the promises in REVERSED order.
- Crash + resume.
- Assert the replay is BIT-IDENTICAL (same step outputs, same promise-id assignment, same child-spawn order).

## Acceptance (the gate)
- `concurrency_spike` PASSES → P5 unblocked (p5-graph/actions/lint/tests may start).
- `concurrency_spike` FAILS → document why; P5 deferred; demote p5-* to backlog; captain re-prioritizes.

## Considerations
- Research, not a feature. Time-box (e.g. 1-2 days). The binary outcome (pass/fail) determines P5's fate.
close_reason: GATE PASS (5/5 deterministic). Resonate SDK 0.4.0 concurrency primitive proven: two concurrent ctx.run().spawn() durable children, both suspending on external ctx.promise(), resolved REVERSED (b before a), worker crashed mid-suspend (verified parked via !handle.done()), fresh worker resumed same run id — replay bit-identical: same step outputs (a->{n:1}, b->{n:2} not swapped), same promise-id assignment (pre-crash sink == post-replay sink), same child-spawn order. Commit 9192b1d. P5 unblocked.

## Scope (the captain's daily dashboard)

- `list` — all runs across crons/workflows: state + owner + **per-run model/token cost (advisory)**.

title: CI: gate SC-11 WF-08 crash-resume (the Resonate differentiator) — currently P2-feature-gated, never runs
description:
# F3 — SC-11 (the WF-08 differentiator test) is never run by CI

## Evidence of defect
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only:
- `cargo test --workspace` (default features)
- `cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p1`

But the decisive test — `crates/toron-e2e/tests/sc11_workflow_approval.rs` — is gated `#![cfg(feature = "p2")]` and the live flywheel integrated-mode test `sc_fw_flywheel_binary_live` is `#[ignore = "requires bd-o8j.2 + flywheel repo checkout"]`.

**The single most important claim of the entire project — 'request_approval suspends, survives a process crash, resumes (Buzz cannot)' — has ZERO CI coverage.** A regression that breaks WF-08 would ship undetected.

## Soundness gap
- **Witness**: SC-11 is a strong witness (real `resonate serve` subprocess, real engine drop, real resume assertion) — but the witness is silent in CI. The claim 'Phase 2 ships' (ADR ordering: workflow+@mention first) is unsupported by the gate.
- The `bd-nks` bead closed claiming 'SC-11 green' — true locally with `--features p2`, invisible to CI.

## Minimum acceptable fix
Add a CI job that runs the P2 e2e suite on every push/PR (not just p1):
```yaml
  e2e-p2:
    name: toron-e2e P2 gate (Resonate differentiator)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Install resonate CLI   # SC-11 spawns `resonate serve`
        run: cargo install resonate --version 0.9.7 || true
      - name: cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p2
        run: cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p2
```
If `resonate` is not installable from crates.io in CI, document the prereq in the README + add a doctor check, and gate SC-11 behind `#[ignore]` ONLY if resonate is absent (with a `TORON_CI_P2` env override to force-run it when present).

## Do NOT broaden into
- Running all `#[ignore]`d tests in CI (some need live flywheel binary — separate concern).
- A federation integration test matrix (out of scope for v1).

## Remediation posture
Narrow CI-config change + 1 doctor-check addition. The differentiator must be gated somewhere repeatable.
close_reason: FIXED: added e2e-p2 CI job to .github/workflows/ci.yml that installs resonate CLI (cargo install resonate --locked) and runs cargo test -p toron-e2e --features p2 on every push/PR. SC-11 (the WF-08 differentiator) is now CI-gated. If resonate install fails the job degrades gracefully (SC-11 self-#[ignore]s when the binary is absent).

title: Addressable replaceable store + projection operator>agent priority
description:
# Task: Addressable/replaceable event semantics (NIP-33) + projection key-priority

## Background
Kinds 30010–30014, 30031, 30032 are parameterized-replaceable. Relay/bus dedup key is `(kind, pubkey, d)`. **Projection** applies an additional rule for toron semantics: for a given `(kind, d)`, latest-wins with **key-priority operator > agent** (A1 force-release).

## What
1. Bus store: ON CONFLICT for addressable keys by author isolation (NIP-33)
2. Projection resolver: merge agent lease + operator revoke with operator priority
3. Document difference: raw relay observers see both events; toron tools see resolved state
4. Unit tests with same `d`, different pubkeys, revoke wins in projection only

## Why
Without this, force-release and profile updates are wrong on federated or multi-writer views.

## Placement
Implement in bus store + projection layer; referenced by reservation/slot/profile tools.
close_reason: bus/addressable.rs: NIP-33 addressable semantics — is_addressable (30000-39999), AddressableKey (kind,pubkey,d), is_revocation (content plain/JSON + status tag), KeyPriority (operator>agent A1), resolve_coordinate (latest-wins within priority class, operator revoke beats newer agent lease). BusEventStore.insert_addressable = author-isolated supersede (same author same (kind,d) replaces; different author survives for projection). 10 tests: kind range, key extraction, latest-wins same/diff authors, operator revoke wins (A1), no-operator = raw view, revocation detection, store supersede + projection resolve. cargo test -p toron-core --lib 142/142 green; clippy+fmt clean

description:
# SC-2 — Direct mail + thread + ack [P1]

## Actors
Pi-α, OC-β

## Steps + assertions (three DISTINCT things — keep them separate)

1. **Parity poll** — Pi-α `mail send --to OCβ --subject review --body … --ack`; then OC-β
   `mail inbox --unread` RETURNS the message (this is a **poll** — AM-Rust parity).
   thread_id = root event id (NIP-10 `e`). The message is queryable in OC-β's projection
   <50ms after send (projection write latency).

2. **Bus push** — a bus/projection subscriber (NOT an MCP client) receives the kind-1059 /
   kind-14 event <50ms after publish; zero polling on the bus path. This is the
   InProcessBus notification (bd-led.3.2) — and per the bd-led.3.2 review note, the
   projection subscriber MUST be on a lossless channel, not a dropping `broadcast`.

3. **MCP subscription push** — validated in bd-led.7.3's OWN acceptance (an rmcp client
   subscribes to `toron://agents/OCβ/inbox`; `send_message` pushes a subscription
   notification <50ms via `subscriptions/listen`, SEP-2575). NOT asserted here — 7.3 owns it.

4. OC-β `mail ack <id>` → Pi-α sees the ack (private NIP-17 to sender, `toron-kind=ack`);
   idempotent on repeat (second ack returns stored ts).

## Assert
- 1 NIP-17 gift-wrap to OC-β; unwraps to a kind-14 rumor.
- Ack is a private NIP-17 to Pi-α (G8); thread_id = root event id.
- Parity-poll (1), bus-push (2), and ack round-trip all hold.
- MCP-subscription-push (3) is bd-led.7.3's contract, not this scenario's.

## Deps
bd-cvp (harness), bd-led.5.3 (messaging tools). Bus-push (2) transitive via

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05):

**1. v1 is now an explicit milestone.** This bead (`bd-wiw`) rolls up the three v1-mandatory epics: bd-led (Phase-1 mailbox+MCP+CLI core), bd-77u (conformance + golden fixtures + CI), bd-o8j (flywheel integrated mode). It could NOT be folded into bd-led directly: bd-77u and bd-o8j transitively depend on bd-led's children (bd-led.7 MCP wiring), so adding them to bd-led would create a cycle (bd-led → bd-77u → bd-led.7 → bd-led). bd-wiw is a cycle-free sink so bv surfaces v1 as the critical-path terminus.

**2. Removed a bad edge.** bd-o8j.3 (P3 remote-daemon fallback) was gating bd-o8j (P1 integrated mode) — a P3 optional must not block the primary 3A deliverable. bd-o8j.3 is now standalone P3.

**3. OPTIONAL de-risk (captain decision, not forced):** the novel core (Nostr bus + NIP-17 gift-wrap + projection parity + MCP) carries real integration risk, and the current plan delivers zero user value until the full 38-tool parity + conformance + CLI + flywheel embed are all done. A non-blocking "preview milestone" — in-process bus + identity + send/fetch/ack messaging exposed over MCP (~8 of 38 tools) — would let the captain dogfood real agent mail weeks earlier and surface architecture bugs before the full parity build. This does NOT descope parity (ADR-locked non-negotiable); it sequences a thin vertical slice first. Accept/reject as a follow-up; if accepted it becomes a P0 bead feeding the first SC smoke (SC-1/SC-2) without adding to the critical path beyond what those already need.

title: NIP-40 envelope TTL 90d + permanent Git content separation
description:
# Task: NIP-40 envelope TTL (90d default) vs permanent Git content

## What
- Gift-wrap / bus envelopes carry NIP-40 `expiration` (default 90 days, config override)
- Bus queries omit expired events
- Git archive of unwrapped content is permanent (no TTL)
- Cleanup job/path for expired envelope GC on InProcessBus SQLite

## Why
Parity superiority: bounded bus growth vs AM-Rust unbounded single store.

## Tests
- Expired envelope not delivered to new subscribers
- Unwrapped mail still in Git after envelope expiry

title: Job lifecycle 43001-06 + @mention + A7 semaphore
description:
# Task: Job lifecycle 43001–43006 Buzz-verbatim + claim semaphore (A7)

## What
- Implement kinds: request/accept/progress/result/cancel/error
- First-claimer wins (signed 43002)
- `dispatch_job`: bounded semaphore + one-in-flight-per-agent
- @mention parser queues 43001

## Tests
- Claim race: only one winner
- Burst @mentions do not thrash (semaphore)
- Federation claim visibility `#[ignore]` multi-process
close_reason: Job lifecycle done in toron-workflow: jobs.rs (builders 43001-43006 Buzz-verbatim with e=parent, wire-identical signed events, first_claimer first-observed-wins on InProcessBus total order, job_state terminal priority result/error/cancel over claim+progress), mention.rs (channel-agnostic @mention parser — mention marker + p tag on kind-14 OR kind-9, per beads-review), dispatch.rs (A7: bounded Semaphore + one-in-flight-per-agent + durable queued mirror, busy-agent jobs stay queued not dropped). 29 tests: claim race single-winner, burst no-thrash, queue durability, terminal states. Federation claim-race #[ignore]/P2.2 documented (InProcessBus total order). Note: workspace gate still red from oc-a bd-2wc persona break in oc-b sc1 + oc-c toron-mcp (not my files, notified).

comments.author: beads-review
comments.text:
Plan-space review (2026-08-05):

1. **@mention parser is channel-agnostic.** The parser keys off a mention marker + `p` tag on ANY message (kind-14 DM OR kind-9 channel msg). So @mention dispatch delivers value in P2.1 BEFORE channels ship — a human DMs "@OCβ fix X" → kind-43001. Channel-mention (SC-9 / bd-l73) is the P2.2 multi-party UX. Don't make the parser channel-bound; that would needlessly hard-depend on bd-esh.2 and break the captain's "workflow+@mention before channels" ordering.

2. **Claim resolution on InProcessBus = first-observed-43002 wins** (the bus is a total order in-process). Federation claim races (two agents claim on different relays simultaneously) are a known hard problem — note it, do NOT try to solve it in P2.1 (Phase 2.1 is InProcessBus; federation RelayBus is later).

3. **Queued jobs are durable.** With the A7 semaphore (bounded concurrency + one-in-flight-per-agent), excess @mentions QUEUE. Queued 43001s persist in the bus event store; on toron restart the dispatcher resumes from the bus cursor (no lost jobs). Consistent with the lossless-projection rule from the bd-led.3.2 review — do not put the dispatch queue on a dropping channel.

- no second toron daemon
- mail latency still push-based
- `rg 'fn agent_prompt'` one definition

flywheel embed (o8j.1) + SC harness patterns; can live in toron-e2e or flywheel tests.
